definition_zh: 铁；熨斗；熨烫；链条（复数）
definition_en: a strong grey metal, a heated tool for smoothing cloth, or the act of pressing clothes with it
core_image: 一块灰黑色的金属锭，旁边放着一台还冒着蒸汽的熨斗
scene: 洗衣房里蒸汽升起，她左手扶着衬衫，右手推着沉重的熨斗走过领口。The old gate is made of iron and has never rusted.
sceneCN: 这里 iron 是「铁」（第 1 个义项：那种金属），句意为这扇老门是铁做的，从来没有生锈。画面里的物件：熨斗、衬衫、蒸汽。

pos.zh: 名词：铁；熨斗；镣铐
动词：熨烫
形容词：铁的；坚强的

collocations.phrase: strike while the iron is hot

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「熨烫；要熨的衣物」
同以 iron 开头的形近词，义为「反讽」，词源不同
由本词加 ware 构成，义为「铁器」

senses.title: The metal
senses.definition: a hard grey metal used for tools, rails, and gates
senses.definitionCN: 一种坚硬灰暗的金属，用于工具、铁轨与大门
senses.example: The bridge was built with iron beams from the old mill.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥用了旧磨坊拆下来的铁梁。
senses.why: The metal sense is the oldest and stays attached to beams, rails, and gates.
senses.whyCN: 金属义最古老，至今仍与梁、轨、门连在一起。

senses.title: The smoothing tool
senses.definition: a flat heated tool used to press wrinkles out of cloth
senses.definitionCN: 一种扁平且加热的工具，用来压平布上的皱褶
senses.example: The iron was still hot when she put it down.
senses.exampleCN: 她放下熨斗时它还是烫的。
senses.why: The tool took the metal name because it was a block of iron heated over a fire.
senses.whyCN: 这个工具之所以借了金属的名字，因为它本是放在火上加热的铁块。

senses.title: Pressing clothes smooth
senses.definition: to press cloth with heat so that it lies flat
senses.definitionCN: 用热量压平布料
senses.example: He ironed his shirt five minutes before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前五分钟他才把衬衫熨好。
senses.why: The verb is simply the tool turned into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义就是把工具名直接变成动作。

senses.title: Chains and firm will
senses.definition: metal restraints, or metaphorically a hard and unyielding quality
senses.definitionCN: 金属镣铐，或比喻坚硬不屈的性质
senses.example: They spoke of the iron discipline of the mountain rescue team.
senses.exampleCN: 他们谈起山地救援队那种铁一般的纪律。
senses.why: From chains to character, the hard metal became a figure for what will not bend.
senses.whyCN: 从镣铐到性格，这种硬金属成了「不肯弯」的象征。

intro.en: Iron is an old Germanic word; its distant origin is uncertain, though Celtic is a strong candidate.
intro.cn: iron 是个古老的日耳曼词，更远的来源不确定，凯尔特语是较有力的候选。

items.en: The word appears as isern or iren in early texts.
items.cn: 这个词在早期文献中写作 isern 或 iren。

items.en: Related forms include German Eisen and Old Saxon isarn.
items.cn: 同源形式包括德语 Eisen 与古撒克逊语 isarn。

items.en: The deeper root may come from a Celtic metal word, but it is disputed.
items.cn: 更深层词根可能来自凯尔特语的金属词，但仍有争议。

items.en: Middle English changed the -s- to -r-, giving iren.
items.cn: 中古英语把 -s- 变成 -r-，写作 iren。

items.en: Modern English settled on iron for both the metal and the tool.
items.cn: 现代英语把 iron 固定下来，兼指金属与熨斗。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the iron spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for metals and pressing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 iron 拼写；近义组收表示金属与压平动作的词。

entries.definition: Saying the opposite of what you mean.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「反讽」，拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: The plural, or chains for a prisoner.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为复数，也可指镣铐。

entries.definition: The activity of pressing clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「熨烫」，同族词。

entries.definition: Iron hardened with carbon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「钢」，铁与碳的合金。

entries.definition: To push down or flatten with force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「压」，压平的动作。

entries.definition: To make a surface even.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「使平整」，结果导向。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie together the metal, the tool, and the act of pressing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把金属、工具和压平这个动作串起来。

normal.en: One word, one metal, one heavy tool.
normal.cn: 一个词，既是金属，也是那件沉工具。

normal.en: An iron is heavy because it is iron.
normal.cn: 熨斗沉，正是因为它就是铁。

normal.en: To iron is to press with that weight.
normal.cn: iron 作动词就是拿这份重量去压。

normal.en: German Eisen is a cousin from the same family.
normal.cn: 德语 Eisen 是同族的表亲。

normal.en: The -r- came late; early English said isern.
normal.cn: 那个 -r- 是后来才有，早先英语说 isern。

abstract.en: Iron is a metal that remembers the shape you give it.
abstract.cn: 铁是会记住你所给形状的金属。

abstract.en: An iron is iron made gentle by heat.
abstract.cn: 熨斗是被热软化过的铁。

abstract.en: Iron will is the metal kept uncooled.
abstract.cn: 铁一般的意志，是不肯冷却的金属。

examples.en: The locket is silver, but the chain is iron.
examples.cn: 坠子是银的，链子却是铁的。

examples.en: She ironed the curtains before hanging them again.
examples.cn: 她先把窗帘熨好再重新挂上。

examples.en: The prisoners wore irons on their ankles.
examples.cn: 囚犯脚踝上带着镣铐。

dict_mnemonic.text: iron 既是铁，也是拿铁做的熨斗，最后成了熨衣服

root: 古英语 isern / iren（日耳曼语词）→ 中古英语 iren → 现代英语 iron。同源有德语 Eisen；更深层来源可能来自凯尔特语，尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the metal, the smoothing tool, pressing clothes, and chains or an unyielding will.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：金属铁、熨斗、熨衣服，以及镣铐或钢铁般的意志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey metal heavy enough to press cloth flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块沉得足以把布压平的灰色金属。

branches.en: THE BEAM: metal bent into bridges and gates.
branches.cn: 铁梁这条线：被弯成桥梁与大门的金属。

branches.en: THE TOOL: the same metal given a handle and heat.
branches.cn: 工具这条线：同一块金属加上把手和热。

branches.en: THE ACT: pressing cloth until wrinkles go.
branches.cn: 动作这条线：把布压到皱褶消失。

branches.en: THE STRENGTH: hardness is both material and metaphor.
branches.cn: 坚硬这条线：硬度既是材质也是比喻。

branches.en: THE HAND: the tool and the act are one idea.
branches.cn: 手这条线：工具和动作本是同一个意思。

intro.en: Iron has no prefix or suffix to cut off; it is a whole Germanic root whose origin is debated.
intro.cn: iron 没有可切分的前后缀，它是一个来源有争议的完整日耳曼词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no secure Latin source, so latinEntries stays empty; Latin ferrum "iron" is unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有可靠的拉丁语来源，所以 latinEntries 留空；拉丁语 ferrum「铁」并不同源。

items.example: It forms irons, also used for chains.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 irons，也用来指镣铐。

items.example: The compound joins iron to ware.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把 iron 与 ware 连起来。
另一个复合词，指一种行当。

items.example: It starts with the same letters but is unrelated in origin.
items.exampleCN: 开头字母相同，却不同源。

items.example: The earlier spelling shows the lost -s-.
items.exampleCN: 较早的写法显示那个消失的 -s-。

items.example: The compound keeps the metal image.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词保留了金属的意象。

definition_zh: 灌溉；灌溉系统；所供之水；医学冲洗；河流对土地的补给；灌区；灌溉农业；灌溉工程学
definition_en: the artificial supply of water to land, or the system, water and practice by which this is done
core_image: 干裂的田垄上，一条新挖的沟把河水一点点引到玉米根部，泥土由灰转深
scene: 正午的田埂上，农人提起闸板，让河水顺着沟流进干裂的玉米地。The farmer lifts the sluice gate and lets river water run down the ditch for irrigation.
sceneCN: 这里 irrigation 指「把水引入农田的行为」（第 1 个义项：人工给土地供水）；句意为农人提起闸板放水，让河水顺着沟流进田里。可辨识物件：田埂、闸板、沟渠、玉米地。

pos.zh: 灌溉；灌溉系统；冲洗

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 irrigare「浇水」的动词形，去掉动作名词后缀 -ation 后得到，语义由「灌溉这一行为」转为「实施灌溉」
基础词 irrigate + -or（拉丁施动者后缀）→ 由「浇水」偏移为「进行灌溉的人或器具」
基础词 irrigate + -able（能力后缀）→ 由「浇水」偏移为「可以灌溉的」
基础词 irrigation + -al（形容词后缀）→ 由「灌溉」偏移为「与灌溉相关的」
micro-（微小）+ irrigation → 由「灌溉」偏移为「微灌，极小尺度的灌溉」
fertilizer 与 irrigation 的混成形式 → 由「灌溉」偏移为「随水施肥」

senses.title: Supply of water to land
senses.definition: the artificial supply of water to fields or crops, usually through channels, pipes or sprinklers
senses.definitionCN: 通过渠道、管道或喷头向农田或作物人工供水
senses.example: Irrigation turned the dry valley into a wheat field.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉把这条干谷变成了麦田。
senses.why: the noun names the action itself, the plainest sense of the Latin verb irrigare 'to water'.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词直接指行为本身，是拉丁动词 irrigare「浇水」最朴素的义项。

senses.title: System of canals and works
senses.definition: the canals, pipes, pumps and channels built to carry water to land
senses.definitionCN: 为把水送到田间而修建的渠道、管道、水泵与沟渠
senses.example: The irrigation of the plain begins at a stone weir upstream.
senses.exampleCN: 这片平原的灌溉从上游一座石堰开始。
senses.why: once the action is repeated at scale, the word shifts from the act to the built works that make it possible.
senses.whyCN: 当这一行为被大规模重复，这个词就从行为转指使行为得以实现的工程设施。

senses.title: Water delivered
senses.definition: the water that is actually delivered to a field, measured in volume or depth
senses.definitionCN: 实际送到田里的水，按体积或深度计量
senses.example: The irrigation for this plot is measured at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地的灌水量在闸口处计量。
senses.why: since the verb means to water, the noun can name the water itself rather than the act of giving it.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词意为浇水，名词也可以指水本身，而不指给水这个动作。

senses.title: Washing a wound or cavity
senses.definition: the flushing of a wound, sinus or body cavity with a stream of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用液流冲洗伤口、窦腔或体腔
senses.example: The nurse recorded the irrigation of the wound in the chart.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把伤口冲洗记录在病历上。
senses.why: medicine borrowed the watering image for washing a body surface with fluid, and the noun followed the verb into that use.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「浇水」这一意象，指用液体冲洗体表，名词也随之进入这一用法。

senses.title: Watering by a river
senses.titleCN: 河流对土地的天然补给
senses.definition: the natural watering of land by a river, flood or rising groundwater
senses.definitionCN: 河流、洪水或上升的地下水对土地的自然浸润
senses.example: The annual irrigation of the floodplain keeps its soil fertile.
senses.exampleCN: 洪泛平原每年的自然浸润使土壤保持肥沃。
senses.why: rivers water their banks without any engineer, and the noun extends to that natural supply.
senses.whyCN: 河流无需工程师也会浸润两岸，名词便延伸到这种天然供水。

senses.title: Irrigated land
senses.definition: the tract of land that is supplied with water by a system, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 由灌溉系统供水的一大片土地，作为整体看待
senses.example: The irrigation of the province covers a hundred thousand hectares.
senses.exampleCN: 该省的灌区覆盖十万公顷土地。
senses.why: the noun can stand for the area that receives the water, since the land is what the whole system exists for.
senses.whyCN: 名词可以指接受供水的整片区域，因为整个系统正是为这片土地而存在。

senses.title: Farming that depends on watering
senses.definition: a way of farming in which crops depend on delivered water rather than on rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 作物依赖输送的水而非降雨的耕作方式
senses.example: Irrigation supports two harvests a year in this district.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉让这个地区一年有两季收成。
senses.why: where rain is unreliable, the practice becomes a whole farming method, and the noun names it.
senses.whyCN: 在雨水不可靠的地方，这种做法成为一整套耕作方式，名词便指这种方式。

senses.title: The engineering field
senses.definition: the branch of engineering and agronomy concerned with designing and managing water delivery
senses.definitionCN: 负责设计与管理输水系统的工程学与农学分支
senses.example: She took a course in irrigation before returning to the family farm.
senses.exampleCN: 她先修了一门灌溉工程课，之后回到家里的农场。
senses.why: a body of technique and theory grows around the practice, and the noun comes to name that field of study.
senses.whyCN: 围绕这一做法生长出一套技术与理论，名词便转而指这个研究领域。

intro.en: Irrigation comes from Latin irrigatio, the noun of action from irrigare 'to water', formed with in- 'into' and rigare 'to moisten'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: irrigation 来自拉丁 irrigatio，是动词 irrigare「浇水」的动作名词，由 in-「进入」与 rigare「润湿」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rigare meant 'to water, moisten'. Its deeper origin is not established; the links suggested with other watering verbs are hypotheses, so any earlier root offered for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: rigare 意为「浇水、润湿」。其更早来源尚无定论；把它与别的「浇水」动词相联系的种种说法都只是假说，因此为它给出的更早词根均属重构形式。

items.en: The prefix in- 'into' combined with rigare to give irrigare 'to lead water into, to water'. The prefix assimilates to ir- before r.
items.cn: 前缀 in-「进入」与 rigare 结合成 irrigare「把水引入、浇水」，前缀在 r 前同化为 ir-。

items.en: Irrigatio was the action noun: the supplying of water, and by extension the works that supplied it.
items.cn: irrigatio 是动作名词，指供水，也引申指供水的设施。

items.en: Medieval Latin kept the word for watering farmland and for washing a body part, and both senses passed into the European languages.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语保留了「浇灌农田」与「冲洗身体部位」两义，二者都传入了欧洲各语言。

items.en: English adopted irrigation in the seventeenth century, first for the watering of land and later for medical flushing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收了 irrigation，先指给土地浇水，后又指医学冲洗。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of rigare is unsettled, and the exact date of its first English use is not recorded, so older forms quoted for it are reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定：rigare 的来源无定论，其英语首见的确切年代也无记录，因此为它引用的更早形式属重构形式而非书证。

note.en: Group one separates the word from its close relatives and from the look-alike irritation, which shares sound but not origin; group two separates it from other water words.
note.cn: 第一组把它与近亲词以及形近而不同源的 irritation 分开；第二组把它与别的「水」类词分开。

entries.definition: The verb names the act; irrigation is the noun of action built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词指动作；irrigation 是在它之上构成的动作名词。

entries.definition: Describes land or a field that has received water; it modifies the object, not the practice.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已受水的土地或田地；它修饰对象，而不指这种做法。

entries.definition: Says of land that can be irrigated; a capacity word, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指土地可以灌溉；这是能力词，不是行为。

entries.definition: From irritare 'to provoke'; it looks and sounds close but has no watering sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 irritare「激怒」；形音都接近，却与水毫无关系。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for giving plants water; irrigation is the large-scale, engineered version.
entries.definitionCN: 给植物供水的日常说法；irrigation 是大规模、有工程的版本。

entries.definition: The removal of water from land; irrigation brings water in, drainage takes it away.
entries.definitionCN: 把水从土地排走；灌溉送水进来，排水把水带走。

entries.definition: Deliberately covering a field with water, one technique of irrigation rather than its name.
entries.definitionCN: 有意让水淹没田面，是灌溉的一种技术，而不是灌溉本身。

entries.definition: Distributing water in drops; it names one delivery method, while irrigation names the whole practice.
entries.definitionCN: 以水滴形式布水；它指一种输送方式，而 irrigation 指整套做法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb, the built works, real fixed phrases and real derived words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁动词、实际工程设施、真实固定搭配与真实派生词。

normal.en: Latin rigare 'to water' plus in- 'into': to lead water into the land.
normal.cn: 拉丁 rigare「浇水」加 in-「进入」：把水引进土地。

normal.en: The family runs irrigate, irrigation, irrigator, irrigable, irrigational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 irrigate、irrigation、irrigator、irrigable、irrigational。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the practice: irrigation canal, drip irrigation, flood irrigation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这种做法：灌溉渠、滴灌、漫灌。

normal.en: The tools have their own names: irrigator for the person or device, irrigable for land that can take water.
normal.cn: 工具另有名称：施动者或器具叫 irrigator，能受水的土地叫 irrigable。

normal.en: The opposite word is drainage, which removes the water that irrigation brings in.
normal.cn: 反方向的词是 drainage，它排走灌溉送来的水。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn in dust with one finger, and water following it to a stalk.
abstract.cn: 想象用手指在尘土里划出一道线，水沿着它流到一株茎前。

abstract.en: Picture a dry field turning dark in bands as each furrow fills.
abstract.cn: 想象干田随着每条沟被灌满，一条条地由灰变深。

abstract.en: Picture a sluice gate lifted by hand, and a whole valley drinking at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手提起闸门，整条山谷同时开始饮水。

examples.en: Ancient irrigation made the first cities possible on land with little rain.
examples.cn: 古老的灌溉让第一批城市得以建在少雨的土地上。

examples.en: The hospital uses irrigation to clean deep wounds before stitching.
examples.cn: 医院在缝合前用冲洗清洁深部伤口。

examples.en: Modern irrigation delivers water drop by drop to save the scarce supply.
examples.cn: 现代灌溉一滴一滴地送水，以节约稀缺的水源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ir-（进入）+ rig（浇水）+ -ation（名词）」——把水引进田里的这件事 → 灌溉

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ rigare「浇水、润湿」→ irrigare「引水入、浇灌」→ irrigatio「供水、灌溉」；rigare 更早来源不确定。英语经法语与晚期拉丁进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the water outward from the act: first the deed and the works, then the water itself, then the borrowed medical wash, then the river's own supply, and finally the land, the farming and the engineering field.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项顺着水从行为向外展开：先是行为与工程，再是水本身，然后是借用的医学冲洗、河流自身的补给，最后是土地、农耕与工程学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ditch cut through dry ground, carrying river water to the roots of a crop.
core.cn: 核心意象：在干地上开出一条沟，把河水送到作物的根部。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS WATER: the deed of giving water and the water that arrives are named by the same noun.
branches.cn: 行为与其水：给水的动作与到达的水由同一个名词命名。

branches.en: WORKS AND CRAFT: channels and pumps turn the act into an engineered system, and then into a field of study.
branches.cn: 工程与技艺：渠道与水泵把行为变成工程系统，再变成一个研究领域。

branches.en: MEDICAL WASH: a fluid stream cleans a wound or cavity, borrowing the watering image.
branches.cn: 医学冲洗：液流清洁伤口或体腔，借用了浇水的意象。

branches.en: RIVER SUPPLY: a river waters its floodplain with no machinery at all.
branches.cn: 河流补给：河流无需任何机械便浸润自己的洪泛平原。

branches.en: LAND AND FARMING: the watered tract, and the farming method that depends on delivered water.
branches.cn: 土地与农耕：受水的那片地，以及依赖输水的耕作方式。

intro.en: Irrigation can be read in parts: an assimilated Latin prefix, a Latin verb of watering, and an action-noun suffix.
intro.cn: irrigation 可按部分读出：一个同化的拉丁前缀、一个表示浇水的拉丁动词，以及一个动作名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is genuine here: irrigare, irrigatio, irrigator and irrigabilis all belong to the same verb, and rigare is the watering root behind them.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的拉丁词族是真实的：irrigare、irrigatio、irrigator 与 irrigabilis 都属同一个动词，rigare 是它们背后的浇水词根。

items.structure: Latin in- 'into', assimilated to ir- before r
items.example: The prefix directs the water inward to the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把水引向田里。

items.example: The root appears again in irrigate and irrigator.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也出现在 irrigate 与 irrigator 中。

items.structure: Latin -atus, past participle and verb ending
items.example: Irrigate is the verb built on the root.
items.exampleCN: irrigate 是在这个词根上构成的动词。

items.example: Irrigation names the act and its result.
Farmers irrigate the fields in spring.

items.meaning: one who or that which irrigates
items.example: The irrigator checks the gate each morning.
items.exampleCN: 灌溉者每天早上检查闸口。

items.example: The lower field is irrigable; the ridge is not.
items.exampleCN: 低处的田可以灌溉，山脊则不行。
灌溉工程改变了这条山谷。

items.meaning: watering on a very small scale

items.example: Fertigation delivers nutrients with the drip line.
items.exampleCN: 水肥一体化让养分随滴灌管送达。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun of action from irrigare
latinEntries.meaning: a watering, a supplying of water
to lead water in, to water

definition_zh: 激怒；使烦躁；刺激（皮肤等）；使发炎
definition_en: to make someone angry or annoyed, or to make a part of the body sore and uncomfortable
core_image: 一根小刺反复蹭着同一块皮肤，人忍不住皱起眉
scene: 巴士晚了半小时，旁边的人一直用鞋跟敲地板。The constant tapping began to irritate everyone in the queue.
sceneCN: 这里 irritate 是「使烦躁」（第 1 个义项：反复刺激引起不耐烦），句意为那不停的敲击开始让排队的每个人都烦躁起来。画面里的物件：鞋跟、地板、排队的栏杆。

pos.zh: 动词：激怒；使烦躁；刺激；使发炎

derivatives.zh: 由 irritate 加 -ion 构成，义为「恼怒；刺激；发炎」
由 irritate 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「恼火的；发炎的」
由拉丁 irritabilis 而来，加 -able 后缀，义为「易怒的」

senses.title: To make someone annoyed
senses.definition: to make someone feel annoyed, often by something small and repeated
senses.definitionCN: 用细小而反复的举动让人不耐烦、恼火
senses.example: Loud chewing at the next desk irritates her every day.
senses.exampleCN: 邻桌大声咀嚼每天都让她烦躁。
senses.why: The Latin verb irritare meant to provoke, and provocation starts with a small repeated prod.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 irritare 本义是「挑动、激怒」，挑动的起点正是一下又一下的小刺。

senses.title: To make a body part sore
senses.definition: to cause a part of the body, especially skin or eyes, to become sore, red, or itchy
senses.definitionCN: 使皮肤、眼睛等部位发红、发痒或不适
senses.example: This wool sweater irritates my neck.
senses.exampleCN: 这件羊毛衫刺得我脖子发痒。
senses.why: The bodily sense grows straight out of the physical prick that the word first named.
senses.whyCN: 身体义直接从这个词最初指的「扎、刺」长出来，皮肤被扎就会发红发痒。

senses.title: To cause inflammation
senses.definition: to make tissue become inflamed or painful, as an injury or substance can
senses.definitionCN: 使组织发炎、疼痛，如外伤或刺激物所致
senses.example: The smoke irritated his lungs during the fire drill.
senses.exampleCN: 消防演习时烟雾刺激得他肺部发炎。
senses.why: Inflammation is the body-level result of repeated irritation, so the verb extends to medicine.
senses.whyCN: 发炎是反复受刺激在身体层面的结果，于是这个词延伸进医学语境。

senses.title: To provoke a reaction
senses.definition: to stir up a feeling or response in someone, often deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 有意激起某人的某种情绪或反应
senses.example: The question irritated a heated argument in the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题在会议里激起了一场激烈争论。
senses.why: Provoking an emotion is the same push as provoking a person, only the target is a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 激起情绪和激怒一个人是同一种「推」，只是对象换成了感受。

senses.title: To bother mechanically
senses.definition: to disturb a device or process slightly so that it stops working smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 轻微干扰装置或过程，使其不能顺畅运行
senses.example: Dust irritated the old printer until it jammed again.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘搅得那台旧打印机又卡纸了。
senses.why: The extended sense keeps the image of a small foreign thing repeatedly rubbing a mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 这个引申义保留了「小异物反复摩擦机械」的画面。

intro.en: Irritate goes back to Latin irritare, "to provoke, excite, exasperate", a verb of uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: irritate 可追到拉丁语 irritare「挑动、激怒」，更深层的来源一般认为不确定。

items.en: irritare meant to provoke or stir up, and irritatus was its past participle.
items.cn: irritare 意为挑动、激起，过去分词是 irritatus。

items.en: The verb also named making something rough or sore, a bodily prick.
items.cn: 这个词还指把东西弄粗糙、弄痛，是一次身体上的刺。

items.en: Church and medical Latin kept irritatio for provocation and bodily soreness.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语的 irritatio 兼指激怒与身体刺痛。

items.en: English took irritate in the sixteenth century for provoking anger.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 irritate，表示激怒。

items.en: The medical sense of inflamed tissue developed alongside the everyday one.
items.cn: 组织发炎的医学义与日常义一起发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin irrit- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for annoying and for stirring feelings.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁词干 irrit-；近义组收表示惹恼和激起情绪的词。

entries.definition: The feeling of being annoyed, or a sore spot on the skin.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「恼怒；刺痛处」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Annoyed, or red and sore.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词转形容词，义为「恼火的；发红的」。

entries.definition: Easily annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 同源形容词，义为「易怒的」，后缀为 -able。

entries.definition: To make someone slightly angry.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「惹恼」，程度比 irritate 轻，来源不同。

entries.definition: To stir someone into a reaction on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「挑动、激起」，强调有意为之。

entries.definition: To disturb or trouble someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「打扰」，更口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin provocation to the everyday wool-collar feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「挑动」走到毛衣领子扎脖子的日常感受。

normal.en: Latin irritare meant to provoke or stir up.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 irritare 意为挑动、激起。

normal.en: The same root gives irritation and irritable.
normal.cn: 同一词根生出 irritation 与 irritable。

normal.en: Be irritated by is the usual passive pattern.
normal.cn: be irritated by 是常见的被动搭配。

normal.en: Skin and eyes are what wool and smoke irritate.
normal.cn: 羊毛与烟刺激的是皮肤和眼睛。

normal.en: An irritating habit is a small thing done again and again.
normal.cn: irritating habit 就是反复做的小动作。

abstract.en: Irritation is a splinter that keeps touching the same spot.
abstract.cn: 烦躁是一根总碰在同一处的木刺。

abstract.en: To irritate is to push a feeling until it answers.
abstract.cn: 激怒就是把一种情绪推到它应答为止。

abstract.en: Every repeated small sound becomes an irritant.
abstract.cn: 每一个反复的小声音都会变成刺激源。

examples.en: He was irritated by the noise from the street.
examples.cn: 他被街上的噪音弄得烦躁。

examples.en: Strong perfume can irritate the eyes and throat.
examples.cn: 浓香水会刺激眼睛和喉咙。

examples.en: The teacher's slow questions irritated the whole class.
examples.cn: 老师慢吞吞的提问让全班都烦了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一日的头痛」—— 每天一点点，把人磨得烦躁

root: 拉丁语 irritare「挑动、激怒」→ irritatus → 英语 irritate。同族有 irritation、irritating、irritable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: annoying a person, sore skin, inflamed tissue, stirred-up feelings, and a slightly disturbed mechanism.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：惹人烦躁、刺激皮肤、使发炎、激起情绪反应，以及轻微搅扰机械。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sharp point rubbing the same place again and again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小尖点反复蹭同一处。

branches.en: THE DESK: a small sound that wears patience down.
branches.cn: 书桌这条线：小声音把耐心磨光。

branches.en: THE COLLAR: wool against skin until it itches.
branches.cn: 领口这条线：羊毛贴着皮肤直到发痒。

branches.en: THE LUNG: smoke turning irritation into inflammation.
branches.cn: 肺这条线：烟把刺激变成发炎。

branches.en: THE MEETING: one question stirring a whole argument.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：一个问题激起全场争论。

branches.en: THE PRINTER: dust making a machine stutter.
branches.cn: 打印机这条线：灰尘让机器打嗝。

intro.en: Irritate is a borrowed Latin verb; English adds only verb endings and noun or adjective suffixes.
intro.cn: irritate 是整体借来的拉丁动词，英语只添了动词词尾与名词、形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives share the irrit- stem, from irritare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词共用 irrit- 词干，源自 irritare。

items.example: The stem of the whole family.
A Romance cousin of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 同一动词的罗曼语亲属。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示主动的形容词
构成表示感受的形容词

definition_zh: 使隔离；使孤立；使分离；（物质）分离出来
definition_en: to separate someone or something from other people or things, or to keep a substance apart from others
core_image: 一个人被划进一个圆圈里，圆圈外的人都退开半步
scene: 病房的门上贴着一张纸，护士只允许一位访客进去。Doctors decided to isolate the patient for several days.
sceneCN: 这里 isolate 是「使隔离」（第 1 个义项：把人或物与他人分开），句意为医生决定把病人隔离几天。画面里的物件：病房门、纸条、访客。

pos.zh: 动词：隔离；孤立；分离；分离出
形容词：孤立的；单独出现的

derivatives.zh: 由 isolate 加 -ion 构成，义为「隔离；孤立」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「偏僻的；孤立的」
由 isolation 加 -ism 构成，义为「孤立主义」
由 isolate 加 -or 构成，义为「隔离器；隔离开关」

senses.title: To keep apart from others
senses.definition: to separate a person, place, or group from others, often for safety or health
senses.definitionCN: 把某人、某地或某群体与他人分开，常出于安全或健康原因
senses.example: The clinic isolated new arrivals for two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把新到的人隔离了两周。
senses.why: The verb was built on Latin insula, an island, so isolating is making an island of someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建在拉丁语 insula「岛」上，隔离就是把人围成一座岛。

senses.title: To feel cut off
senses.definition: to make someone feel alone and unable to take part in what others do
senses.definitionCN: 使某人在情感上孤独，无法参与他人的活动
senses.example: The language barrier isolated him at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 语言障碍让他在聚会上很孤立。
senses.why: Social isolation repeats the same ring of water, now made of language and custom.
senses.whyCN: 社会层面的孤立还是那一圈水，只是换成了语言和习惯。

senses.title: To separate a part
senses.definition: to take one part or element away from the rest so it can be examined
senses.definitionCN: 把其中一部分或一个要素从整体中取出来单独研究
senses.example: Engineers isolated the faulty wire from the system.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把故障电线从系统里单独分离出来。
senses.why: Separating one element is like lifting one island out of a larger land mass.
senses.whyCN: 把一个要素单拿出来，就像从一整块陆地里抬出一座岛。

senses.title: To obtain a pure substance
senses.definition: to obtain a substance in a pure form, free of everything mixed with it
senses.definitionCN: 得到纯净的物质，去掉其中混杂的其它成分
senses.example: Chemists isolated the active compound from the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家从叶子中分离出了活性化合物。
senses.why: The chemistry sense is the physical version of taking one thing out of a mixture.
senses.whyCN: 化学义是「从混合物中取出一样东西」的物理版本。

senses.title: Standing alone in grammar
senses.definition: describing a language or word form that has no clear relatives or partners
senses.definitionCN: 描述没有明确亲属关系或搭配形式的语言或词形
senses.example: The dialect is an isolated form with no close relatives.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言是一种没有近亲的孤立形式。
senses.why: In linguistics the island image turns into a form with no bridges to anything else.
senses.whyCN: 在语言学里，岛的意象变成了没有任何桥梁可通的形式。

intro.en: Isolate was formed in English in the early nineteenth century from the Latin adjective insulatus, "made into an island".
intro.cn: isolate 是十九世纪初英语造出的词，源自拉丁语形容词 insulatus「被围成岛的」。

items.en: insula meant island and also named a block of flats.
items.cn: insula 意为岛，也指一栋公寓楼。

items.en: insulatus meant made into an island, set apart.
items.cn: insulatus 意为被围成岛的、被隔开的。

items.en: Italian isolato, isolated, gave the verb its -ate shape.
items.cn: 意大利语 isolato「被隔离的」给了这个词 -ate 的形状。

items.en: French isoler appears in the eighteenth century with the same meaning.
items.cn: 法语 isoler 在十八世纪出现，意义相同。

items.en: English formed the verb isolate, and the chemistry sense came in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语造出动词 isolate，化学义在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the insul- or isol- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for separating and excluding.
note.cn: 形近组共用 insul-、isol- 词干；近义组收表示分开与排斥的词。

entries.definition: The state of being separated from others.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「隔离状态」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Relating to an island, or narrow in outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 同源形容词，义为「岛屿的；心胸狭窄的」。

entries.definition: A small island, now mostly in names.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「小岛」，是借入的缩短形式，同族。

entries.definition: To protect something with a barrier.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「隔热、绝缘」，词干同为 insul-。

entries.definition: A very small island.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「小岛」，由 isle 加指小词尾构成。

entries.definition: Cut off from others.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「被隔离的；偏僻的」。

entries.definition: To divide things from each other.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「分开」，最中性，来源不同。

entries.definition: To keep people or animals apart for a period to stop disease.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「检疫隔离」，专用于防疫。

entries.definition: To keep groups apart, often unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「分开、隔离」，常含制度性歧视。

normalIntro.en: These hooks trace isolate back through Italian isolato to the Latin word for island.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 isolate 经意大利语 isolato 追到拉丁语的「岛」。

normal.en: Latin insula meant island.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 insula 意为岛。

normal.en: Italian isolato meant isolated.
normal.cn: 意大利语 isolato 意为被隔离的。

normal.en: Isolation is the noun built with -ion.
normal.cn: isolation 是加 -ion 构成的名词。

normal.en: Doctors isolate patients to stop infection.
normal.cn: 医生隔离病人以阻断感染。

normal.en: An isolated house stands far from any neighbour.
normal.cn: isolated house 指远离任何邻居的房子。

abstract.en: To isolate is to draw a small island around something.
abstract.cn: 隔离就是在某样东西外面画一座小岛。

abstract.en: What is isolated has no bridge to the rest.
abstract.cn: 被孤立的东西没有通往其余部分的桥。

abstract.en: A pure substance is an island taken out of a mixture.
abstract.cn: 纯净物是从混合物里取出的一座岛。

examples.en: The village was isolated by the heavy snow.
examples.cn: 大雪使这个村子与外界隔绝。

examples.en: Scientists isolated a new enzyme from the soil.
examples.cn: 科学家从土壤中分离出一种新的酶。

examples.en: He felt isolated during his first month abroad.
examples.cn: 他在国外的第一个月感到很孤立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱苏累他」—— 把他一个人圈起来，只剩自己

root: 拉丁语 insula「岛」→ insulatus「被围成岛的」→ 意大利语 isolato → 法语 isoler → 英语 isolate。同族有 isolation、insular、insulate。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: keeping people apart, social loneliness, separating a part, obtaining a pure substance, and an isolated language form.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：把人隔开、社交孤独、分出部分、取得纯净物质，以及孤立的语言形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person inside a drawn circle with everyone stepping back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被圈在圆里，别人都退开半步。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: a patient kept behind a closed door.
branches.cn: 诊所这条线：病人被留在关着的门后。

branches.en: THE PARTY: a language barrier that leaves one man silent.
branches.cn: 聚会这条线：语言障碍让一个人沉默。

branches.en: THE WIRE: one faulty part lifted out of a system.
branches.cn: 电线这条线：从系统里单独取出的故障件。

branches.en: THE LEAF: an active compound taken out pure.
branches.cn: 叶子这条线：纯取出来的活性化合物。

branches.en: THE DIALECT: a form with no near relatives.
branches.cn: 方言这条线：没有近亲的语言形式。

intro.en: Isolate comes from the Latin island stem plus a verb ending borrowed through Italian and French.
intro.cn: isolate 来自拉丁语的「岛」词干，再经意大利语与法语各加动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin insula "island" supplies the stem insul-, whose relatives share the shape of something enclosed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 insula「岛」提供词干 insul-，其同族词都带有「被围起来」的形状。

items.example: Italian isolato gave the verb its shape.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语 isolato 给了动词形状。
英语写作 isolate，而非 isolat。

definition_zh: 问题；议题；（报刊的）期号；（证券的）发行；发出；流出
definition_en: a subject people discuss or worry about, one set of printed copies, or the act of officially giving or sending something out
core_image: 水从闸门缝里涌出来，人群围住它讨论该怎么办
scene: 会议室的白板上写满条目，争论渐渐集中到同一行字上。Everyone agreed the main issue was money.
sceneCN: 这里 issue 是「问题、议题」（第 1 个义项：需要讨论或解决的事），句意为大家都认为主要问题在于钱。画面里的物件：白板、条目、会议桌。

pos.zh: 名词：问题；议题；期号；发行
动词：发出；发布；供给
动词：流出；产生于

derivatives.zh: 由 issue 加 -ance 构成，义为「发行；签发」
由 issue 加 -er 构成，义为「发行人」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「已发行的；已签发的」

senses.title: A subject to discuss
senses.definition: an important topic that people are discussing or arguing about
senses.definitionCN: 人们正在讨论或争论的重要话题
senses.example: Housing is the biggest issue in this election.
senses.exampleCN: 住房是这次选举中最大的问题。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a going out or a flowing forth, and a disputed question is what flows out into public talk.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思有「流出」，而值得争论的问题正是从人群里流出来的话题。

senses.title: A problem to solve
senses.definition: a difficulty or problem that needs to be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理的困难或麻烦
senses.example: We have an issue with the water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的供水出了问题。
senses.why: A problem is a question that has begun to leak, so the outflow image turns into trouble.
senses.whyCN: 麻烦就是开始漏水的那个问题，流出的画面变成了故障。

senses.title: One set of printed copies
senses.definition: a single set of a newspaper or magazine published at one time
senses.definitionCN: 报纸或杂志一次出版的全部内容
senses.example: The May issue has a long article on bees.
senses.exampleCN: 五月那一期有一篇关于蜜蜂的长文。
senses.why: Each copy flows out from the press on one day, so the noun names one release.
senses.whyCN: 每一批印品在一天里从印刷机流出，于是这个名词指一次发行。

senses.title: To give out officially
senses.definition: to officially give something such as a document, ticket, or warning to people
senses.definitionCN: 正式把文件、票据或警告等交给别人
senses.example: The office issued new passes to all visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室向所有访客发出了新通行证。
senses.why: Issuing sends something out from an authority, exactly the going-out of the Latin source.
senses.whyCN: 签发是权威把东西送出去，正是词源里「向外走」的意思。

senses.title: To flow out
senses.definition: to come or flow out from a place or an opening
senses.definitionCN: 从某处、某开口流出来
senses.example: Water issued from a crack in the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 水从墙上的裂缝里流出。
senses.why: This is the oldest bodily sense, kept in modern technical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义，保留在现代技术性描述里。

senses.title: To result from
senses.definition: to come or result from a particular cause or source
senses.definitionCN: 由某个原因或来源产生
senses.example: Her doubts issue from an earlier failure.
senses.exampleCN: 她的疑虑源自更早的一次失败。
senses.why: Something that comes out of a source is the same movement as water out of a gap.
senses.whyCN: 从来源出来，与从缺口出水是同一种移动。

intro.en: Issue comes from Latin exire, "to go out", through its past participle exitus, "a going out".
intro.cn: issue 来自拉丁语 exire「出去」，经其过去分词 exitus「出去、出口」进入古法语。

items.en: exire meant to go out, from ex, out, and ire, to go.
items.cn: exire 意为出去，由 ex「向外」与 ire「走」组成。

items.en: exitus meant a going out, an end, or an outlet.
items.cn: exitus 意为出去、结果或出口。

items.en: Old French issue named an outlet, a way out, or a result.
items.cn: 古法语 issue 指出口、出路或结果。

items.en: English adopted issue for an exit and later for something sent out.
items.cn: 英语先以 issue 表示出口，后来表示送出的东西。

items.en: Printing made issue mean one release of a periodical, and the debate sense followed.
items.cn: 印刷出版让 issue 指一期刊物，讨论话题的义项随之出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the exit or issu- shape; the near-meaning group holds words for topics, problems, and sending out.
note.cn: 形近组共用 exit、issu- 形状；近义组收表示议题、问题与发出的词。

entries.definition: A way out or the act of leaving.
entries.definitionCN: 与 issue 同为拉丁 exire 的后代，义为「出口；离开」。

entries.definition: The act of officially issuing something.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ance 构成，义为「发行；签发」。

entries.definition: The material of which body parts are made.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「组织」，拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The subject of a talk or text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「主题」，偏中性的讨论对象。

entries.definition: A difficulty that needs solving.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「难题」，比 issue 更直接。

entries.definition: To give things out to many people.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「分发」，与 issue 的发出义相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the Latin going-out verb to magazines, tickets, and arguments.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语「出去」的动词走到杂志、票据与争论。

normal.en: Latin exire means to go out.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 exire 意为出去。

normal.en: exitus means a going out or an outlet.
normal.cn: exitus 意为出去或出口。

normal.en: An issue of a magazine goes out on one day.
normal.cn: 一期杂志在一天里发行出去。

normal.en: To issue a ticket is to hand it out officially.
normal.cn: issue a ticket 就是正式发出票据。

normal.en: The main issue is what everyone argues about.
normal.cn: main issue 就是大家都在争的那件事。

abstract.en: An issue is a subject that leaks out of a group.
abstract.cn: 议题是从人群里漏出来的话题。

abstract.en: A problem is an issue with its lid off.
abstract.cn: 麻烦是揭了盖子的议题。

abstract.en: What issues from a source was inside it before.
abstract.cn: 从来源流出的东西，原本就在里面。

examples.en: Privacy is a serious issue for many users.
examples.cn: 隐私对许多用户来说是严重的问题。

examples.en: The bank will issue a new card next week.
examples.cn: 银行下周会发行一张新卡。

examples.en: Smoke issued from the vents on the roof.
examples.cn: 烟从屋顶的通风口里冒出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一休」—— 一休思考的正是那个大问题

root: 拉丁语 exire「出去」（ex 向外 + ire 走）→ exitus「出去；出口」→ 古法语 issue → 英语 issue。同族有 exit、issuance、issuer。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a topic under discussion, a difficulty, one release of a periodical, official giving out, flowing out, and resulting from.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：讨论的议题、麻烦、一期刊物、正式发出、流出，以及出自某来源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water slipping out of a gate while a crowd argues about it.
core.cn: 核心意象：水从闸门缝里涌出，人群围着它争论。

branches.en: THE ELECTION: one topic everyone keeps returning to.
branches.cn: 选举这条线：人人反复回到的那个话题。

branches.en: THE PIPE: a leak that has become trouble.
branches.cn: 水管这条线：漏成了麻烦。

branches.en: THE BEES: one month of a magazine leaving the press.
branches.cn: 蜜蜂这条线：从印刷机出来的一期杂志。

branches.en: THE PASS: a document handed out at a desk.
branches.cn: 通行证这条线：在窗口发出去的文件。

branches.en: THE CRACK: water out of a gap, doubt out of a failure.
branches.cn: 裂缝这条线：水从缺口出，疑虑从失败出。

intro.en: Issue is a French reshaping of the Latin noun exitus; only English endings are later additions.
intro.cn: issue 是古法语对拉丁名词 exitus 的改写，后面加的英语词尾是后来才有的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all turn on ex-, out, and ire, to go.
latinIntro.cn: 这些拉丁同族词都围绕 ex-「向外」与 ire「走」。

items.example: Combined with ire it forms exire.
items.exampleCN: 与 ire 结合构成 exire。

items.example: The base verb of the family.

items.exampleCN: 法语写作 issue，而非 exite。

items.example: It forms issue date and issue number.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 issue date 与 issue number。

definition_zh: 项目；条款；一件物品；一条新闻
definition_en: a single thing in a list, group, or set, or one piece of news in a report
core_image: 清单上一行一行的小格子，每格只放一件东西
scene: 超市的收银台上，收银员把篮子里的东西一件件拿出来扫描。Each item was scanned and bagged in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 item 是「一件物品」（第 1 个义项：清单里单列的一样东西），句意为每件物品几秒内就扫完装袋。画面里的物件：收银台、购物篮、扫描枪。

pos.zh: 名词：项目；条款；一件物品；一条新闻

derivatives.zh: 由 item 加 -ize 构成，义为「逐项列出」
由 itemize 加 -ation 构成，义为「逐项列明」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「逐项列出的」

senses.title: One thing in a set
senses.definition: a single object among a number of similar things, especially in a shop or a set
senses.definitionCN: 一批同类东西中的单独一件，常用于商店或成套物品
senses.example: Every item in the box was checked twice.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子里的每件物品都查了两遍。
senses.why: The word began as a single entry in a list, and a thing in a shop is one such entry.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指清单上的单独一条，商店里的那件东西正是这样一条。

senses.title: A point on a list
senses.definition: one point or entry in a list, agenda, or order of business
senses.definitionCN: 清单、议程或议事程序中的一条
senses.example: The first item on the agenda is the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 议程上的第一项是预算。
senses.why: The list sense is the oldest one, and each numbered line is still an item.
senses.whyCN: 清单义最古老，每一条编号的行仍然叫 item。

senses.title: A clause in a document
senses.definition: one separate article or clause in a contract, law, or set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 合同、法律或规章中单独的一条
senses.example: Item three of the contract sets the payment date.
senses.exampleCN: 合同第三条规定了付款日期。
senses.why: A legal clause is a list entry written by lawyers, so the same word fits.
senses.whyCN: 法律条款是律师写下的清单条目，于是同一个词也适用。

senses.title: One piece of news
senses.definition: a short single report in a newspaper, broadcast, or news feed
senses.definitionCN: 报纸、广播或信息流中单独的一条报道
senses.example: A short news item mentioned the bridge closure.
senses.exampleCN: 一条短新闻提到了那座桥封闭的消息。
senses.why: A news page is a list of reports, and each report is one item on it.
senses.whyCN: 新闻版面就是一串报道，每篇都是上面的一条。

senses.title: Two people as a couple
senses.definition: used in old-fashioned or humorous speech for two people known to be a couple
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或玩笑说法，指大家知道的一对情侣
senses.example: They are an item again after the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天过后他们又成了一对。
senses.why: A couple becomes a single entry in gossip, so two people are listed as one thing.
senses.whyCN: 一对情侣在闲谈里变成一个条目，于是两个人被当成一样东西列出来。

intro.en: Item is the Latin word item, meaning "likewise, in the same way", used to begin each separate entry in a list.
intro.cn: item 就是拉丁语 item「同样地」，原本用在清单每一条的开头，后来被当成那一条本身。

items.en: item was an adverb meaning likewise or also.
items.cn: item 是副词，意为同样地、也。

items.en: In lists and accounts each line began with item, so the word marked one entry.
items.cn: 在清单和账簿里每一行都以 item 开头，于是这个词标记一条记录。

items.en: Old French took item as a noun for an entry in a list.
items.cn: 古法语把 item 用作名词，指清单里的一条。

items.en: English borrowed it for a statement in an account or inventory.
items.cn: 英语借来指账目或清册中的一项。

items.en: The meaning widened from list entry to any single thing.
items.cn: 词义从清单条目扩展到任何单独的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ite-/item- shape; the near-meaning group holds words for single things and list entries.
note.cn: 形近组共用 ite-、item- 形状；近义组收表示单件物品与清单条目的词。

entries.definition: To list things one by one.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ize 构成，义为「逐项列出」，同族动词。

entries.definition: The plural of item.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，义为「多个项目」，同族。

entries.definition: The pronoun for a thing already named.
entries.definitionCN: 代词义为「它」，拼写只是开头相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A written piece, or one clause of a document.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「文章；条款」，与 item 的条款义重叠。

entries.definition: A physical thing that can be seen and touched.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「物品」，只指实物。

entries.definition: One record written in a list or book.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「条目」，强调写下来的记录。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the Latin adverb item to the supermarket counter and the agenda.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语副词 item 走到超市收银台与会议议程。

normal.en: Latin item meant likewise or also.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 item 意为同样地、也。

normal.en: Each line of an old list began with item.
normal.cn: 旧清单的每一行都以 item 开头。

normal.en: Itemize means to put things into items.
normal.cn: itemize 就是把东西逐项列出来。

normal.en: A news item is one report in a bulletin.
normal.cn: news item 就是简报里的一条报道。

normal.en: Item by item means one thing at a time.
normal.cn: item by item 意为一项一项地。

abstract.en: An item is a box that holds exactly one thing.
abstract.cn: item 是只装一样东西的小格子。

abstract.en: A list is a row of boxes, each called an item.
abstract.cn: 清单就是一排格子，每个格子叫一项。

abstract.en: Two people who are an item share one box.
abstract.cn: 成为一对的两个人共用一个格子。

examples.en: Please list each item on a separate line.
examples.cn: 请把每一项分行列出。

examples.en: The last item on the agenda was the new office.
examples.cn: 议程最后一项是新办公室。

examples.en: She counted every item in the delivery.
examples.cn: 她清点了这批货里的每一件物品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一件」—— 清单上就一件一件地数

root: 拉丁语副词 item「同样地；也」→ 清单每行开头的标志 → 古法语 item「一条」→ 英语 item「项目；一件」。同族有 itemize、itemization。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: one object in a set, a point on a list, a legal clause, one piece of news, and a couple.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：成套物品中的一件、清单上的一项、法律条款、一条新闻，以及一对情侣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of small boxes, one thing in each.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列小格子，每格只放一样东西。

branches.en: THE COUNTER: each thing scanned once.
branches.cn: 收银台这条线：每样东西各扫一次。

branches.en: THE AGENDA: numbered points in order.
branches.cn: 议程这条线：按顺序编号的事项。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT: one clause with a number.
branches.cn: 合同这条线：带编号的那一条。

branches.en: THE BULLETIN: a single short report.
branches.cn: 简报这条线：单独的一条短报道。

branches.en: THE GOSSIP: two names written as one entry.
branches.cn: 闲谈这条线：两个名字写成一个条目。

intro.en: Item is a borrowed Latin word; English adds only -ize and noun endings.
intro.cn: item 是借来的拉丁词，英语只在后面加 -ize 与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives are forms of the same adverb and its noun use.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词就是这个副词及其名词用法的形式。

items.example: The mark at the start of each line.
Readers took the marker for the entry itself.
items.exampleCN: 读者把这个标记当成了条目本身。

items.example: It forms itemal in older legal writing.
items.exampleCN: 旧法律文本里构成 itemal。

items.example: It forms item number and item price.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 item number 与 item price。

latinEntries.meaning: the head of a new entry

definition_zh: 颌；下巴；（字面或比喻）下颚；（工具）钳口
definition_en: either of the two bones or parts that form the mouth and hold the teeth, or a gripping part of a tool
core_image: 一张脸的下半部，上下两排牙齿像两把钳子合上
scene: 老人慢慢嚼着面包，脸上的颌骨一起一落。His jaw moved slowly as he chewed.
sceneCN: 这里 jaw 是「颌」（第 1 个义项：构成嘴部、承载牙齿的骨或部位），句意为他咀嚼时下颌慢慢动着。画面里的物件：面包、牙齿、老年斑的皮肤。

pos.zh: 名词：颌；下巴；钳口
动词：喋喋不休（口语）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「上下颌」，也指机构的夹钳
由 jaw 加 -ed 构成，义为「有……颌的」，见于 long-jawed 等复合词
由 jaw 与 bone 复合，义为「颌骨」

senses.title: The bone that holds teeth
senses.definition: one of the two bony structures that form the frame of the mouth and hold the teeth
senses.definitionCN: 构成嘴部框架并承载牙齿的两块骨结构之一
senses.example: He broke his lower jaw in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛中摔断了下颌。
senses.why: The anatomical sense is the oldest and stays the basis for every later use.
senses.whyCN: 解剖义最古老，也是后来所有用法的基础。

senses.title: The lower part of the face
senses.definition: the lower part of the face, seen especially when it is large or firm
senses.definitionCN: 脸的下部，尤其指宽大或坚硬的形态
senses.example: A square jaw ran across the whole bottom of his face.
senses.exampleCN: 宽方的下巴横过他的脸底。
senses.why: The bone shapes the face, so people name the visible outline by the bone beneath.
senses.whyCN: 骨头撑出脸的形状，于是人们用底下的骨来称呼那道外轮廓。

senses.title: A gripping part of a tool
senses.definition: one of the two parts of a vice or wrench that close on an object
senses.definitionCN: 老虎钳或扳手上合拢夹物的两片之一
senses.example: Tighten the jaws of the vice around the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 把老虎钳的钳口夹紧管道。
senses.why: A tool grips with two facing surfaces exactly as a mouth bites with two jaws.
senses.whyCN: 工具用两片相对的面夹住东西，与嘴用上下颌咬住一模一样。

senses.title: Something that closes in
senses.definition: a dangerous opening or closing area, such as between waves or between rocks
senses.definitionCN: 危险的开合处，如巨浪之间或岩石之间
senses.example: The boat slipped into the jaws of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 小船滑进了风暴的夹口。
senses.why: The mouth image grows into any wide, closing gap that swallows what enters.
senses.whyCN: 嘴的意象扩大成任何张开又合拢、把东西吞进去的缺口。

senses.title: To talk on and on
senses.definition: used informally for talking at length, often about nothing important
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示长时间讲话，常指说些不重要的事
senses.example: They jawed about football all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整晚都在聊足球。
senses.why: The verb turns the jaw that does the working into the act of talking.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个干活的颌变成了说话这个动作。

intro.en: Jaw is an old French borrowing, from Old French joue, meaning cheek, reshaped in English toward the sound it names.
intro.cn: jaw 是从古法语借来的词，原形 joue 意为「面颊」，在英语里逐渐定型为现在的读音与拼写。

items.en: joue meant a cheek.
items.cn: joue 意为面颊。

items.en: English took the word as jawe or chaw, and it meant the part that holds teeth.
items.cn: 英语借入为 jawe 或 chaw，指承载牙齿的部位。

items.en: The spelling drifted toward jaw and the meaning settled on the bone.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐变成 jaw，词义固定在骨头上。

items.en: The tool sense appeared as machines with gripping parts spread.
items.cn: 随着带夹持部件的机器普及，工具义出现。

items.en: The informal verb to jaw, meaning to chatter, is recorded from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 口语动词 jaw「喋喋不休」在十九世纪有记录。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jaw- family; the near-meaning group holds words for mouth parts and gripping tools.
note.cn: 形近组是 jaw- 词族；近义组收嘴部器官与夹持工具相关词。

entries.definition: The two jaws, or a gripping pair.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，义为「上下颌」，也指成对的夹口。

entries.definition: The bone of the jaw.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「颌骨」，同族名词。

entries.definition: So surprising that the mouth falls open.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「令人瞠目结舌的」。

entries.definition: The part of the face below the mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「下巴尖」，只指最外边的一点。

entries.definition: The side of the face below the eye.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「面颊」，jaw 的古法语原义就是它。

entries.definition: A curved gripping part on an animal or tool.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「爪」，指弯曲的夹持部位。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Old French cheek into the bone, the vice, and the storm.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从古法语的「面颊」走到骨头、老虎钳与风暴。

normal.en: Old French joue meant a cheek.
normal.cn: 古法语 joue 意为面颊。

normal.en: English kept the sound and moved the meaning to the bone.
normal.cn: 英语保留了读音，把词义移到了骨头上。

normal.en: A vice has two jaws that close on a pipe.
normal.cn: 老虎钳有两只钳口夹住管道。

normal.en: The jaws of the storm swallow small boats.
normal.cn: 风暴的夹口会吞掉小船。

normal.en: To jaw with friends is to talk for hours.
normal.cn: to jaw with friends 就是聊上几个小时。

abstract.en: A jaw is a clamp built into a face.
abstract.cn: 颌就是长在脸上的一把钳子。

abstract.en: Teeth close; so does a wrench.
abstract.cn: 牙齿会合上，扳手也会。

abstract.en: What opens wide will one day close.
abstract.cn: 张得很大的东西总有一天会合拢。

examples.en: He rubbed his jaw where the ball had hit him.
examples.cn: 他揉了揉被球打中的下巴。

examples.en: The crocodile opened its jaws and waited.
examples.cn: 鳄鱼张开嘴等着。

examples.en: They stood jawing at the corner for an hour.
examples.cn: 他们在街角站着聊了一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爪」—— 上下颌像一对爪子把食物抓住

root: 古法语 joue「面颊」→ 中古英语 jawe／chaw「承载牙齿的部位」→ 现代英语 jaw「颌；下巴；钳口」。同族有 jaws、jawbone、jaw-dropping。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the bone that holds teeth, the visible lower face, a tool's gripping part, a closing gap, and talking at length.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：承载牙齿的骨、可见的下半脸、工具的夹持部位、张合的缺口，以及长篇闲聊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the lower half of a face closing two rows of teeth like pliers.
core.cn: 核心意象：脸的下半部，两排牙齿像钳子一样合上。

branches.en: THE MATCH: a lower jaw broken by a fall.
branches.cn: 比赛这条线：摔断的下颌。

branches.en: THE FACE: a square outline under the skin.
branches.cn: 脸这条线：皮下那道方方的轮廓。

branches.en: THE VICE: two steel jaws on a pipe.
branches.cn: 老虎钳这条线：夹住管道的两片钢口。

branches.en: THE SEA: storm jaws around a small boat.
branches.cn: 海这条线：围住小船的暴风夹口。

branches.en: THE CORNER: two friends talking through the evening.
branches.cn: 街角这条线：两人聊过整个晚上。

intro.en: Jaw is a French borrowing reshaped in English; the later forms are English compounds and endings.
intro.cn: jaw 是法语借词在英语里改定的，较晚的形式都是英语复合与词尾。

latinIntro.en: The source is Old French, not Latin, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是古法语而非拉丁语，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.exampleCN: 有文献记载的法语来源。

definition_zh: 爵士乐；爵士舞；爵士风格；（口语）活力、花样
definition_en: a style of music with strong rhythm and free improvisation, developed by African American musicians
core_image: 小号手闭着眼，音符从乐器里甩出去，鼓手在旁跟着改动节奏
scene: 午夜的小酒吧里，几个人轮流即兴，观众用脚打拍子。The band played jazz until two in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 jazz 是「爵士乐」（第 1 个义项：以强烈节奏与即兴为特点的音乐），句意为乐队一直演奏爵士乐到凌晨两点。画面里的物件：酒吧、小号、鼓、打拍的脚。

pos.zh: 名词：爵士乐；活力；花样
动词：（口语）使其更热闹；即兴演奏

derivatives.zh: 由 jazz 加 -y 构成，义为「爵士风格的；花哨的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「兴奋的」
由 jazz 与 man 复合，义为「爵士乐手」

senses.title: The music itself
senses.definition: a style of music with strong rhythm, swing, and a large share of improvisation
senses.definitionCN: 节奏强烈、摇摆感明显、即兴成分很大的音乐风格
senses.example: Jazz was born in the southern United States.
senses.exampleCN: 爵士乐诞生于美国南部。
senses.why: The musical sense is the core of the word and the source of every other meaning.
senses.whyCN: 音乐义是这个词的核心，也是其他意义之源。

senses.title: The style attached to it
senses.definition: the manner, dress, or way of playing that belongs to jazz performance
senses.definitionCN: 属于爵士演奏的方式、穿着或风格
senses.example: The cafe has a jazz feel with dark wood and warm lights.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆用深色木头和暖灯营造出爵士味。
senses.why: A style can be named by the music it evokes, even when no music is playing.
senses.whyCN: 即使不放音乐，一种风格也可以借它唤起的音乐来命名。

senses.title: A dance to that music
senses.definition: a lively dance performed to jazz music, later a stage dance form
senses.definitionCN: 随爵士乐跳的活泼舞蹈，后来发展成舞台舞种
senses.example: Students learn jazz in the dance class.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在舞蹈课上学习爵士舞。
senses.why: Dancing grew with the music, and the name travelled with the rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈随音乐一同成长，名字也随着节奏一起走。

senses.title: Liveliness or energy
senses.definition: an informal use for energy, excitement, or a lively quality in something
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，指活力、兴奋或某种生动特质
senses.example: The new colours gave the room some jazz.
senses.exampleCN: 新的色彩给房间添了些活力。
senses.why: Jazz as lively music becomes a word for liveliness itself.
senses.whyCN: 爵士乐这种活泼的音乐，本身就成了「活泼」的代称。

senses.title: To make lively
senses.definition: to add decoration or energy to something so that it becomes more interesting
senses.definitionCN: 给某物增添装饰或活力，使其更有趣
senses.example: They jazzed up the menu for the holiday season.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为节日季把菜单做得更花哨。
senses.why: The verb takes the lively quality of the noun and hands it to another thing.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词里那股活泼劲儿交到别的东西身上。

intro.en: Jazz appeared in print around 1912 for baseball slang and by the late 1910s for music; its deeper origin is still disputed.
intro.cn: jazz 约在 1912 年出现在报纸上是棒球俚语，到 1910 年代末指音乐，更深层的来源至今仍有争议。

items.en: Early records of jazz describe energy and liveliness, not yet music.
items.cn: 早期记录里的 jazz 指精力旺盛、活泼，还不是音乐。

items.en: The word spread from California newspapers in the late 1910s.
items.cn: 这个词在 1910 年代末从加州报纸传开。

items.en: New Orleans bands took jazz as the name of their music around 1917.
items.cn: 新奥尔良的乐队约在 1917 年用 jazz 称呼他们的音乐。

items.en: The music came from African American communities, including brass bands and blues.
items.cn: 这种音乐来自非裔美国人社群，包括铜管乐队与蓝调。

items.en: Jazz became a word for its style and later for liveliness in general.
items.cn: jazz 先成为风格之名，后来又泛指活泼。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jazz- family; the near-meaning group holds music styles and related performance words.
note.cn: 形近组是 jazz- 词族；近义组收音乐风格与演出相关词。

entries.definition: In the style of jazz, or bright and showy.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「爵士风的；花哨的」。

entries.definition: A musician who plays jazz.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「爵士乐手」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Very excited.
entries.definitionCN: 口语形容词，义为「兴奋的」。

entries.definition: A slow sad music form from African American tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「蓝调」，节奏更慢、情绪更沉。

entries.definition: A strong rhythmic style related to jazz.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「摇摆乐」，是爵士的近亲风格。

entries.definition: To make up music as you play it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「即兴演奏」，是爵士的核心手法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the slang sense of energy to the New Orleans bands.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从俚语里的「活力」走到新奥尔良的乐队。

normal.en: Jazz began as US slang for liveliness.
normal.cn: jazz 起初是美国俚语，指活力。

normal.en: New Orleans bands named the music jazz around 1917.
normal.cn: 新奥尔良乐队约在 1917 年把这种音乐叫作 jazz。

normal.en: Jazzy means in the style of jazz, or showy.
normal.cn: jazzy 意为爵士风的，或花哨的。

normal.en: Jazz up means to give something more life.
normal.cn: jazz up 意为给某物添生气。

normal.en: The deeper origin of jazz is still unknown.
normal.cn: jazz 更深层的来源至今不明。

abstract.en: Jazz is music that changes while you listen.
abstract.cn: 爵士是你听着它就在变的音乐。

abstract.en: A horn throws a line, and the drums answer back.
abstract.cn: 号甩出一句，鼓接回一句。

abstract.en: Liveliness itself can be called jazz.
abstract.cn: 活泼劲儿本身也可以被叫作 jazz。

examples.en: She listens to jazz while she works.
examples.cn: 她工作时听爵士乐。

examples.en: The festival mixes jazz with local folk songs.
examples.cn: 这个音乐节把爵士乐与当地民歌混在一起。

examples.en: They jazzed up the old hall with bright lights.
examples.cn: 他们用明快的灯光让旧礼堂热闹起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎兹」—— 音一扎一响，就是即兴摇摆的味儿

root: 美国俚语 jazz（约 1912 年出现，初指活力）→ 1910 年代末从西海岸报纸传开 → 1917 年前后新奥尔良乐队用于音乐 → 二十世纪扩展为风格与「活力」义。同族有 jazzy、jazzman。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the music, its style, the dance, liveliness, and the verb of making something livelier.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：爵士乐、其风格、爵士舞、活力，以及使更有生气的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trumpeter improvising while the drummer answers him.
core.cn: 核心意象：小号手即兴，鼓手在旁边回应。

branches.en: THE BANDS: brass, blues, and a rhythm section.
branches.cn: 乐队这条线：铜管、蓝调与节奏组。

branches.en: THE CAFE: dark wood and warm lights with no music playing.
branches.cn: 咖啡馆这条线：深木与暖灯，却不放音乐。

branches.en: THE STUDIO: dancers learning a swing step.
branches.cn: 舞蹈室这条线：学员模仿摇摆步。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a little colour that wakes it up.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：一点让人醒过来的颜色。

branches.en: THE MENU: ornaments added for a festival.
branches.cn: 菜单这条线：为节日添上的花样。

intro.en: Jazz is a modern American coinage or slang borrowing; the additions below are ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: jazz 是近代美国造词或俚语借词，下面的添加成分都是普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Jazz has no Latin source, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: jazz 没有拉丁语来源，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: It forms jazz band and jazz club.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jazz band 与 jazz club。

definition_zh: 嫉妒的；羡慕的；吃醋的；小心守护的
definition_en: unhappy because someone has something you want, or afraid of losing someone's love or attention
core_image: 有人朝你喜欢的人伸出手，你不由地把杯子握得更紧
scene: 聚会上有人和她聊了很久，他在角落里一直盯着那只杯子。He felt jealous when she laughed with his old friend.
sceneCN: 这里 jealous 是「嫉妒的」（第 1 个义项：因别人得到自己想要的东西而不快），句意为她和他的老朋友说笑时他感到嫉妒。画面里的物件：聚会的杯子、角落、旁人的笑声。

pos.zh: 形容词：嫉妒的；吃醋的；小心守护的

derivatives.zh: 由 jealous 加 -y 构成，义为「嫉妒；吃醋」
由 jealous 加 -ly 构成，义为「嫉妒地；小心地」
由 jealous 加 -ness 构成，义为「嫉妒的状态」

senses.title: Wanting what another has
senses.definition: unhappy and resentful because someone else has something you want
senses.definitionCN: 因别人拥有你想要的东西而不快、怨恨
senses.example: He was jealous of her new car.
senses.exampleCN: 他嫉妒她的新车。
senses.why: This sense grows from the older fear of rivals and is now the commonest use.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项从更古老的「害怕情敌」延伸出来，如今最常用。

senses.title: Afraid of losing love
senses.definition: afraid that someone you love might be more interested in another person
senses.definitionCN: 害怕所爱的人对别人更有兴趣
senses.example: She gets jealous if he talks for long to anyone else.
senses.exampleCN: 只要他跟别人聊久了，她就会吃醋。
senses.why: The rival's jealousy is the oldest thread, kept in the emotional sense we still use.
senses.whyCN: 提防情敌的嫉妒是最古老的一条线，保存在我们今天仍在用的情感义里。

senses.title: Guarding possessively
senses.definition: very careful to protect something you think of as yours
senses.definitionCN: 非常谨慎地守护自己认为是自己的东西
senses.example: The manager is jealous of his team's time.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理很爱惜团队的时间。
senses.why: Guarding closely is the same grip on what one considers one's own, with anger removed.
senses.whyCN: 紧守不放是对「自己之物」的同一种握紧，只是抽掉了愤怒。

senses.title: Envying with respect
senses.definition: admiring another person's good fortune in a way that is slightly painful
senses.definitionCN: 带着一点痛感地羡慕别人的好运
senses.example: I am jealous of your long holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 我羡慕你那么长的假期。
senses.why: In everyday speech the word now covers mild envy as well as resentment.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语里，这个词既指怨恨，也涵盖轻微的羡慕。

senses.title: Protective of an idea
senses.definition: unwilling to let a right or principle be weakened
senses.definitionCN: 不肯让自己的权利或原则被削弱
senses.example: They were jealous of their independence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们非常珍视自己的独立。
senses.why: A community guarding its rights watches them as closely as a jealous keeper guards a door.
senses.whyCN: 守护权利的群体，就像小心看守门的守卫一样看得极紧。

intro.en: Jealous came through Old French gelos from Greek zelos, then Latin zelus, meaning eager rivalry or zeal.
intro.cn: jealous 经古法语 gelos 来自希腊语 zelos、拉丁语 zelus，原义为热烈争胜或热忱。

items.en: zelos meant eager rivalry, zeal, or jealousy.
items.cn: zelos 意为热烈的争胜、热忱或嫉妒。

items.en: zelus kept the same range of eager feeling.
items.cn: zelus 保留了同样一串热切的情感义。

items.en: gelos narrowed the word toward jealousy and love.
items.cn: gelos 把词义收窄到嫉妒与爱情上。

items.en: English took jelus or gelous as an adjective.
items.cn: 英语借入 jelus、gelous 作形容词。

items.en: The same Greek root also gave zeal and zealous.
items.cn: 同一个希腊词根还生出 zeal 与 zealous。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jealous family and the zealous cousin; the near-meaning group holds envy and suspicion.
note.cn: 形近组是 jealous 词族与 zealous 这一同源近亲；近义组收羡慕与猜疑相关词。

entries.definition: The feeling of being jealous.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -y 构成的名词，义为「嫉妒」。

entries.definition: In a jealous or watchful way.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「嫉妒地；小心地」。

entries.definition: Full of energy for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 同源形容词，义为「热心的」，词根同为希腊 zelos。

entries.definition: Wanting what another person has.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「羡慕的、嫉妒的」，更侧重羡慕。

entries.definition: Not trusting someone's honesty.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「多疑的」，强调不信任。

entries.definition: Wishing to control someone's attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「占有欲强的」，常用于关系。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie jealous to the Greek root that also produced zeal and zealous.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 jealous 系到同样生出 zeal、zealous 的希腊词根上。

normal.en: Greek zelos meant eager rivalry.
normal.cn: 希腊语 zelos 意为热烈争胜。

normal.en: Zeal and zealous share the same root.
normal.cn: zeal 与 zealous 共用同一词根。

normal.en: Jealous of is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: jealous of 是常见的搭配。

normal.en: Old French gelos pointed the word at love.
normal.cn: 古法语 gelos 把词义指向爱情。

normal.en: To guard jealously is to watch very closely.
normal.cn: guard jealously 就是看得极紧。

abstract.en: Jealousy counts what someone else is holding.
abstract.cn: 嫉妒在数别人手里有的东西。

abstract.en: The tight hand on a cup is the whole feeling.
abstract.cn: 把杯子握紧的那只手就是全部感受。

abstract.en: Watching a door and watching a person look alike.
abstract.cn: 看住门和看住一个人，动作是一样的。

examples.en: She was jealous of her sister's success.
examples.cn: 她嫉妒姐姐的成功。

examples.en: Try not to get jealous when he talks to others.
examples.cn: 他跟别人说话时尽量别吃醋。

examples.en: The country is jealous of its independence.
examples.cn: 这个国家珍视自己的独立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「急了吗」—— 看见别人有，急得直咬牙

root: 希腊语 zelos「热烈争胜；热忱」→ 拉丁语 zelus → 古法语 gelos「嫉妒」→ 中古英语 jelus → 现代英语 jealous。同族有 jealousy、jealously，同源近亲 zeal、zealous。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: wanting another's goods, fearing a rival in love, guarding one's own, mild envy, and valuing a right.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：想要别人之物、怕爱人被抢、守护自己的东西、轻微羡慕，以及珍视某种权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tightening on a cup while someone reaches toward a friend.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人朝你的朋友伸手，你把杯子握得更紧。

branches.en: THE CAR: a new car shining in a neighbour's drive.
branches.cn: 新车这条线：邻居车道上发亮的新车。

branches.en: THE PARTY: a long talk with an old friend.
branches.cn: 聚会这条线：跟老朋友的长时间闲聊。

branches.en: THE TEAM: a manager protecting working hours.
branches.cn: 团队这条线：经理护着工作时间。

branches.en: THE HOLIDAY: a long break that is envied.
branches.cn: 假期这条线：让人羡慕的长假。

branches.en: THE COUNTRY: independence watched day and night.
branches.cn: 国家这条线：日日夜夜守着的独立。

intro.en: Jealous is an adjective borrowed through French; English adds the noun, adverb, and -ness endings.
intro.cn: jealous 是经法语借入的形容词，英语在后面加了名词、副词和 -ness 词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin zelus, from Greek zelos, is the source; its English relatives include zeal and zealous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 zelus（源自希腊 zelos）是源头，其英语同族包括 zeal 与 zealous。

items.example: The Latin form of the Greek word.
The French form borrowed into English.

items.exampleCN: 它是英语形容词的词尾。

items.example: A cousin from the same root.

definition_zh: 喷气式飞机；喷射；喷嘴；（液体或气体的）一股
definition_en: a fast aircraft driven by jet engines, or a strong narrow stream of liquid or gas forced out of a small opening
core_image: 一股水从细口喷出，笔直射得很远
scene: 机场跑道上一架飞机加速，机尾拉出一条长烟。The jet climbed into the clouds within a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 jet 是「喷气式飞机」（第 1 个义项：靠喷气发动机高速飞行的飞机），句意为一分钟内那架喷气机就爬升进了云层。画面里的物件：跑道、机尾的烟、云层。

pos.zh: 名词：喷气式飞机；喷射；喷嘴；一股
动词：乘喷气机飞行；喷出
形容词：喷气式的；乌黑发亮的

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「喷出的；乘喷气机旅行的」
由 jet 加 -ing 构成，义为「喷射」
与 jet 同源的借词，义为「突堤；码头」

senses.title: A stream forced out
senses.definition: a strong narrow stream of liquid or gas pushed out of a small opening
senses.definitionCN: 从细口被压出的一股强而窄的液体或气体
senses.example: A jet of steam rose from the kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 水壶里喷出一股蒸汽。
senses.why: The stream sense is the oldest, from a French verb meaning to throw out.
senses.whyCN: 射流义最古老，来自法语里表示「抛出」的动词。

senses.title: The nozzle itself
senses.definition: the small opening or pipe through which such a stream comes out
senses.definitionCN: 喷出这股流的细口或管子
senses.example: Clean the jet under the tap.
senses.exampleCN: 在水龙头下把喷嘴冲干净。
senses.why: The opening is named by what comes out of it, a common shift in English.
senses.whyCN: 开口借由从它出来的东西得名，这是英语里常见的转义。

senses.title: An engine that pushes by gas
senses.definition: an engine that produces forward thrust by forcing hot gas backward
senses.definitionCN: 把高温气体向后喷出来获得推力的发动机
senses.example: The jet of the plane roared during take-off.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机起飞时喷气发动机轰鸣起来。
senses.why: The machine works exactly by making a jet, so the word names engine and aircraft together.
senses.whyCN: 这台机器正是靠制造射流工作，于是这个词同时指发动机和飞机。

senses.title: An aircraft with such engines
senses.definition: a plane driven by jet engines, especially a fast passenger plane
senses.definitionCN: 由喷气发动机驱动的飞机，尤指快速客机
senses.example: They took a jet to the coast for the weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 他们周末坐喷气机去了海边。
senses.why: In everyday speech jet means the plane itself, the machine standing for the whole object.
senses.whyCN: 日常语里 jet 就指飞机本身，机器代指了整个物件。

senses.title: Deep glossy black
senses.definition: used before a colour word, especially black, for a deep shining shade
senses.definitionCN: 用在颜色词前，尤其 black，表示深沉发亮的颜色
senses.example: Her hair was jet black in the light.
senses.exampleCN: 她的头发在光下乌黑发亮。
senses.why: The dark shiny lignite called jet gave this colour sense through stone jewellery.
senses.whyCN: 一种叫 jet 的乌黑光亮褐煤，通过石饰带来了这个颜色义。

intro.en: Jet for a stream comes from French jeter, "to throw", from Latin jactare; the black stone jet is a separate word.
intro.cn: 表示射流的 jet 来自法语 jeter「投掷」，其根是拉丁语 jactare；乌黑的宝石 jet 则是另一个词。

items.en: jactare meant to throw or toss repeatedly.
items.cn: jactare 意为反复投掷、抛。

items.en: jeter meant to throw or cast.
items.cn: jeter 意为投、抛。

items.en: English formed jet as the stream thrown out.
items.cn: 英语造出 jet，指被抛出的那一股。

items.en: jet came to name the nozzle and later the pushing action of gas.
items.cn: jet 先指喷嘴，后来指气体向后推的动作。

items.en: The jet engine gave the word its aircraft sense.
items.cn: 喷气发动机给了这个词「飞机」义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jet- family; the near-meaning group holds words for planes and streams.
note.cn: 形近组是 jet- 词族；近义组收飞机与射流相关词。

entries.definition: A structure built out into the water.
entries.definitionCN: 与 jet 同源的名词，义为「突堤；码头」。

entries.definition: Sprayed out, or travelled by jet.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「喷出的；乘喷气机的」。

entries.definition: The act of sending out a stream.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「喷射」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Any flying machine, with or without jet engines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「飞机」，最中性的统称。

entries.definition: Liquid scattered in fine drops.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「喷雾」，比 jet 更散。

entries.definition: A continuous flow of liquid or gas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「流」，比 jet 更宽、更连续。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the throwing verb into nozzles and airports, keeping the black stone apart.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从「投掷」的动词走到喷嘴和机场，并把乌黑宝石那条线分开。

normal.en: French jeter means to throw.
normal.cn: 法语 jeter 意为投、抛。

normal.en: Latin jactare means to toss about.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jactare 意为反复抛掷。

normal.en: A jet of water shoots from a small hole.
normal.cn: 一股水从小孔射出。

normal.en: A jet engine pushes gas backward to go forward.
normal.cn: 喷气发动机把气体向后喷以获得向前的推力。

normal.en: Jet black comes from the shiny black stone jet.
normal.cn: jet black 来自乌黑光亮的宝石 jet。

abstract.en: A jet is a narrow line of liquid that refuses to spread.
abstract.cn: 射流是一道拒绝散开的窄线。

abstract.en: What pushes gas back is pushed forward.
abstract.cn: 往后推气的东西自己被往前推。

abstract.en: A stream and a stone share a spelling but not a history.
abstract.cn: 一股流与一块宝石拼写相同，来历却不同。

examples.en: A jet of hot water hit the wall.
examples.cn: 一股热水冲到了墙上。

examples.en: The jet crossed the Atlantic in six hours.
examples.cn: 这架喷气机六小时飞越大西洋。

examples.en: She wore a jet black dress.
examples.cn: 她穿了一条乌黑的裙子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「急特」—— 气急急地特快一喷，飞得又高又快

root: 拉丁语 jactare「反复投掷」→ 古法语 jeter「投、抛」→ 英语 jet「射流；喷嘴」→ 喷气发动机与喷气机。乌黑宝石 jet 另出一源。同族有 jetted、jetting、jetty。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a forced stream, the nozzle, a jet engine, a jet aircraft, and deep glossy black.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：被压出的射流、喷嘴、喷气发动机、喷气式飞机，以及乌黑发亮的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard straight line of water shot from a small hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：从细孔射出的又直又硬的一股水。

branches.en: THE KETTLE: steam hissing out of a hole.
branches.cn: 水壶这条线：蒸汽从孔里嘶出来。

branches.en: THE TAP: a small nozzle rinsed clean.
branches.cn: 水龙头这条线：冲干净的喷嘴。

branches.en: THE RUNWAY: roaring gas lifting a plane.
branches.cn: 跑道这条线：轰鸣的气体把飞机抬起来。

branches.en: THE LIGHT: shining black hair.
branches.cn: 光这条线：乌黑发亮的头发。

branches.en: THE JEWELLER: the same black stone sold in a shop window.
branches.cn: 珠宝商这条线：橱窗里出售的同一块黑石。

intro.en: Jet is a French borrowing from a Latin verb of throwing; English added the verb endings and compounds.
intro.cn: jet 是古法语借来的词，源头为拉丁语「投掷」动词，英语补上动词词尾与复合。

latinIntro.en: Latin jactare, an intensified form of jacere, supplies the stem behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jactare（jacere 的加强形式）提供了这个词背后的词干。

items.example: The core noun of the entry.

definition_zh: 关节；接缝；共同的；合办的
definition_en: a place where two parts of a body or structure are connected, or something shared by two or more people
core_image: 两根木条在拐角处被一个榫头接住，那儿可以弯
scene: 木工把两根长条拼成一张矮凳，接头处特意留了一点松动。The table is held together by wooden joints, no nails.
sceneCN: 这里 joint 是「接缝」（第 2 个义项：两个构件相接的部位），句意为这张桌子靠木接缝拼成，不用一根钉子。画面里的物件：木条、榫头、矮凳。

pos.zh: 名词：关节；接缝；大块烤肉
形容词：共同的；合办的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「共同地」
同词根的动词，义为「连接；加入」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「有关节的」
加前缀 dis- 构成，义为「脱节的；不连贯的」

senses.title: A body joint
senses.definition: the place where two bones meet and allow movement
senses.definitionCN: 两块骨头相接并能活动的地方
senses.example: He hurt the joint of his thumb in the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他的拇指关节被门夹伤了。
senses.why: Anatomy used the word first in English, for the points where bones meet.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最先用它的就是解剖，指骨头相接的地方。

senses.title: A place where parts meet
senses.definition: the point where two pieces of wood or metal are fitted together
senses.definitionCN: 两块木头或金属相嵌合的地方
senses.example: The pipe leaked at the joint near the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那根管子靠墙的接头处漏水。
senses.why: Carpenters and plumbers borrowed the same word for made joins.
senses.whyCN: 木匠和水管工借同一个词来说人造的接合。

senses.title: Shared by two or more
senses.definition: made or held together by two or more parties
senses.definitionCN: 由两方或多方一起做或一起持有的
senses.example: They run a joint shop and split the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他们合开一家店，房租分摊。
senses.why: The adjective sense moves from physical joining to shared ownership.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义从物理连接挪到共同拥有。

senses.title: A large cut of meat
senses.definition: a piece of meat for roasting, usually with the bone still in
senses.definitionCN: 用于烤制的一块肉，通常带骨
senses.example: Sunday meant a joint of beef and a long table.
senses.exampleCN: 星期天意味着一条烤牛腿和一张长餐桌。
senses.why: A roast joint is the piece carved at the table, where the family joins.
senses.whyCN: 烤大块肉是要在桌上切开的那块，一家人正是在那儿连起来。

intro.en: Joint comes from Latin junctus, "joined", the past participle of jungere, "to join".
intro.cn: joint 来自拉丁语 junctus「已连接的」，是 jungere「连接」的过去分词。

items.en: jungere meant "to join, to yoke together".
items.cn: jungere 意为「连接、套上轭」。

items.en: The past participle junctus meant "joined".
items.cn: 过去分词 junctus 意为「已连接的」。

items.en: French turned it into joint, naming the place of meeting.
items.cn: 法语把它变成 joint，指相接之处。

items.en: Middle English used joint for bones and for carpentry.
items.cn: 中古英语用 joint 指骨头与木作。

items.en: The shared sense grew from "joined together" into business use.
items.cn: 「连在一起」逐渐扩展出商务上的「共同」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the join- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for connections and sharing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 join- 词干；近义组收表示连接与共有的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to connect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「连接」，同词根。

entries.definition: Together, by two or more parties.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「共同地」，同族词。

entries.definition: Lacking connection or order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不连贯的」，加前缀 dis-。

entries.definition: A line where two pieces are sewn or joined.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「缝」，多指布料。

entries.definition: Used or held by more than one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「共有的」，偏所有权。

entries.definition: Felt or done by each towards the other.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「相互的」，偏态度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word at a point where two things touch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它放在两物相触的那一点上。

normal.en: jungere means join, and junctus means joined.
normal.cn: jungere 是连接，junctus 是已连接。

normal.en: A joint is where the joining shows.
normal.cn: joint 就是接合显现出来的地方。

normal.en: Remove the joint and the parts fall apart.
normal.cn: 把这个接点去掉，部件就散了。

normal.en: Bones, planks, and bank accounts all have joints.
normal.cn: 骨头、木板、银行账户都有「接头」。

normal.en: Jointly means the two are joined in acting.
normal.cn: jointly 就是两方连着一起做。

abstract.en: A joint is the hinge where one thing becomes two.
abstract.cn: 接缝是一物分成两物的那处铰链。

abstract.en: Bodies and agreements both fail at the joint.
abstract.cn: 身体和协议，都容易在连接处出问题。

abstract.en: Shared work bends better than separate work.
abstract.cn: 共同的事，比分开的事更会弯。

examples.en: His ankle joint still aches after the fall.
examples.cn: 摔倒之后他的踝关节还疼。

examples.en: The chair needs a new wooden joint at the back.
examples.cn: 这把椅子的后部需要换一个木接缝。

examples.en: The two cities opened a joint fire service last year.
examples.cn: 两座城市去年开设了合办的消防服务。

dict_mnemonic.text: join（连接）+ t —— 两块东西连起来的那一点

root: 拉丁语 jungere「连接」→ junctus「已连接的」→ 古法语 joint → 中古英语 joint。同族有 join、jointly、junction、conjunction。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a bone joint, a fitted seam, something shared, and a cut of meat.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：骨头关节、构件接缝、共同持有的，以及一大块肉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hinge where two pieces meet and can move.
core.cn: 核心意象：两件东西相接并能活动的那处铰链。

branches.en: THE BODY: bones meeting where movement happens.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：能活动的骨相接处。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: wood and pipe fitted at a seam.
branches.cn: 手艺这条线：木头与管子在缝处相嵌。

branches.en: THE DEAL: two parties holding one thing.
branches.cn: 交易这条线：两方持有一物。

branches.en: THE TABLE: a joint of meat at a shared meal.
branches.cn: 餐桌这条线：一顿共餐上的一大块肉。

branches.en: THE LINK: all senses are a place where two become one.
branches.cn: 连接这条线：所有义项都是两物合一之处。

intro.en: Joint is the Latin past participle ending -t on the root joining-; the word itself is borrowed whole.
intro.cn: joint 是词根 joining- 加拉丁过去分词词尾 -t，整词直接从法语借来。

latinIntro.en: Latin jungere and junctus are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jungere 与 junctus 均有记载。

items.example: The root also appears in junction and adjoin.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 junction 与 adjoin。
它把 junctus 标为「已连接」。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。
这个分词给了 joint 那个 -t。

items.example: Same root with a different ending.

definition_zh: 日报；杂志；期刊；日志；日记
definition_en: a magazine or newspaper on a serious subject, or a daily written record of what happens
core_image: 一叠按日期装订起来、纸边写满小字的册子
scene: 图书馆的报刊区，一排放着硬壳合订本，书脊上印着年份。She published her first paper in a medical journal last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 journal 是「期刊」（第 1 个义项：定期出版的专门刊物），句意为她去年春天在医学期刊上发表了第一篇论文。画面里的物件：图书馆、合订本、书脊。

pos.zh: 名词：期刊；杂志；日志；日记

derivatives.zh: 由 journal 加 -ist 构成，义为「新闻工作者」
由 journalist 加 -ism 构成，义为「新闻业；新闻学」
由 journalist 加 -ic 构成，义为「新闻业的」
由 journal 加 -ed 构成，义为「记入日志的」（英式双写 l）

senses.title: A periodical on a special subject
senses.definition: a periodical, often containing serious articles, published for a profession or field
senses.definitionCN: 为某一行业或领域出版的定期刊物，多载严肃文章
senses.example: Her study appeared in a well-known journal.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究发表在一份知名期刊上。
senses.why: The periodical sense grew out of the idea of something issued day by day.
senses.whyCN: 期刊义是从「按日发行」这个概念长出来的。

senses.title: A daily newspaper
senses.definition: a newspaper published every day, now mostly in formal or older usage
senses.definitionCN: 每天出版的报纸，现在多用于正式或较早的语境
senses.example: The news was read aloud from the local journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息是从当地日报上念出来的。
senses.why: A newspaper issued every day takes its name straight from the daily book.
senses.whyCN: 日报每天发行，名字直接来自「每日的簿册」。

senses.title: A personal daily record
senses.definition: a book in which a person writes down events and thoughts each day
senses.definitionCN: 每天记下事情与想法的本子
senses.example: She has kept a journal since she was ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她十岁起就记日记。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is a book kept day by day by one person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层，是一个人按天记下的本子。

senses.title: A log of an activity
senses.definition: an official record of what is done, as in a ship or a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 对所做之事的正式记录，如船上或实验室的记录
senses.example: The engineer noted the fault in the engine journal.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把这个故障记在了轮机日志里。
senses.why: A ship or a lab keeps the same day book, but for duty rather than feeling.
senses.whyCN: 船上或实验室也记同样的日簿，只是记的是职责而不是心情。

senses.title: A published volume of papers
senses.definition: a volume collecting the proceedings or papers of a learned society
senses.definitionCN: 汇集某学会会议记录或论文的册子
senses.example: The society prints its journal every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会每季度印行自己的汇编。
senses.why: Issuing papers at fixed dates turns a day book into a journal for a whole field.
senses.whyCN: 按固定日期印行论文，把日簿变成面向整个领域的期刊。

senses.title: A travel account
senses.definition: a written account of travels, usually kept day by day
senses.definitionCN: 通常按天记录下来的行旅文字
senses.example: His travel journal became a small book.
senses.exampleCN: 他的旅行日志后来成了一本小书。
senses.why: Travellers keep the same daily habit, so the word follows them on the road.
senses.whyCN: 旅人保留同样的按天记录习惯，这个词就跟着他们上路。

intro.en: Journal comes from French journal, a daily book, which descends from Latin diurnalis, "of the day".
intro.cn: journal 来自法语 journal「每日的书」，其源头是拉丁语 diurnalis「每日的」。

items.en: diurnus meant of the day, from dies, a day.
items.cn: diurnus 意为「白日的」，源自 dies「日」。

items.en: diurnalis was the adjective built on diurnus.
items.cn: diurnalis 是由 diurnus 构成的形容词。

items.en: Old French journal meant daily, and also a daily record or book.
items.cn: 古法语 journal 既指「每日的」，也指每日的记录或簿册。

items.en: English adopted journal for a daily account and later for a newspaper.
items.cn: 英语借入 journal 指每日记述，后来又指报纸。

items.en: The learned periodical sense became dominant in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 学术期刊义在十八世纪占据主导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journal stem; the near-meaning group holds other periodicals and records.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journal 词干；近义组收其他刊物与记录。

entries.definition: A person who writes for newspapers or broadcast.
entries.definitionCN: 由 journal 加 -ist 构成，指新闻工作者。

entries.definition: The work or study of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「新闻业；新闻学」。

entries.definition: A trip from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，义为「旅程」，源自同一拉丁「日」词根但路线不同。

entries.definition: A magazine published at regular intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指定期刊物。

entries.definition: A book of daily personal notes.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人的日记本，更私人。

entries.definition: An official record of events.
entries.definitionCN: 技术上指正式运行记录。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from Latin dies, a day, to the library shelf of bound volumes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「日」走到图书馆那排合订本。

normal.en: The root is dies, day, also seen in diary and diurnal.
normal.cn: 词根是 dies「日」，也见于 diary 与 diurnal。

normal.en: Journalist adds -ist to the periodical noun.
