normal.cn: journalist 是给期刊名词加 -ist。

normal.en: Keep a journal is the personal use, at home.
normal.cn: keep a journal 是家里的私人用法。

normal.en: An academic journal is the professional use.
normal.cn: academic journal 是专业领域的用法。

normal.en: Jour and dies both survive in French and Latin day words.
normal.cn: 法语 jour 与拉丁 dies 都是「日」的词。

abstract.en: A journal is a day pressed flat into pages.
abstract.cn: 期刊就是把一天压平成纸页。

abstract.en: The same word holds a scholar and a schoolgirl.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既装着学者也装着女学生。

abstract.en: Bound volumes are years standing on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 合订本就是站在书架上的一整年。

examples.en: The journal publishes four issues a year.
examples.cn: 这本期刊一年出四期。

examples.en: He writes in his journal before sleep.
examples.cn: 他睡前写日志。

examples.en: Her article appeared in an academic journal.
examples.cn: 她的文章登在一份学术期刊上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 jour 日」加「nal」—— 每天一页，就是日志

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnus「白日的」→ diurnalis → 古法语 journal「每日的；日志」→ 英语 journal。同族 diary、journalist、journey。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a specialist periodical, a daily paper, a personal diary, a log, a society volume, and a travel account.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：专业期刊、日报、个人日记、运行日志、学会汇编，以及旅行游记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pages bound by dates, one day after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：按日期订起来的纸页，一天接一天。

branches.en: THE LIBRARY SHELF: issues bound into yearly volumes.
branches.cn: 书架这条线：各期合订成年卷。

branches.en: THE NEWS STAND: a paper that comes every morning.
branches.cn: 报摊这条线：每天早上来的报纸。

branches.en: THE DESK DRAWER: a private day book and a travel tale.
branches.cn: 抽屉这条线：私人的日记与行旅记述。

branches.en: THE ENGINE ROOM: an official log of faults.
branches.cn: 轮机舱这条线：正式记录的故障。

branches.en: THE PEER REVIEW: the gate where research is published.
branches.cn: 同行评议这条线：研究发表的关口。

intro.en: Journal carries the Latin day root di- and takes English endings for its family.
intro.cn: journal 带着拉丁「日」词根 di-，词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from dies, a day, through diurnalis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词经由 diurnalis 来自 dies「日」。

definition_zh: 记者；新闻工作者
definition_en: a person who writes news stories or reports events for a newspaper, magazine, or broadcast service
core_image: 一个人抱着本子挤在人群最前面，边问边记
scene: 雨里围着警戒线，几个人举着手机和录音笔追问路人。A journalist asked the same question three different ways.
sceneCN: 这里 journalist 是「记者」（第 1 个义项：为媒体采写报道的人），句意为一位记者把同一个问题换着问了三种说法。画面里的物件：录音笔、本子、警戒线。

pos.zh: 名词：记者；新闻工作者

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加 -ism 构成，义为「新闻业」
由本词词干加 -ic 构成，义为「新闻的」
由词根直接构成，义为「期刊；日记」
同源于 jour「日」的形近词，义为「旅程」

senses.title: Reporter for the news
senses.definition: a person whose job is to gather facts and write or broadcast the news
senses.definitionCN: 以收集事实并写成或播出新闻为职业的人
senses.example: A journalist from the local paper rang to check the date.
senses.exampleCN: 当地报纸的一位记者打电话来核对日期。
senses.why: The word grew out of journal, a daily record, so a journalist is literally a day-writer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 journal「每日记录」长出来，字面上就是「写日子的人」。

senses.title: Writer of opinion and features
senses.definition: a person who writes longer pieces, comment, or interviews for a publication
senses.definitionCN: 为刊物撰写长文、评论或访谈的人
senses.example: She works as a journalist for a monthly science magazine.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家科学月刊做撰稿人。
senses.why: As papers grew, the job widened from daily reports to any written news work.
senses.whyCN: 随着报纸增多，这个职业从每日报道扩展到各种文字新闻工作。

intro.en: Journalist is journal, "a daily record", plus -ist; its root is the Latin word for day.
intro.cn: journalist 是 journal「每日记录」加 -ist，其词根是拉丁语的「日」。

items.en: dies meant "day".
items.cn: dies 意为「日」。

items.en: diurnalis meant "daily".
items.cn: diurnalis 意为「每日的」。

items.en: jour kept the day sense; journal named a daily book.
items.cn: jour 保留「日」，journal 指每日的记录簿。

items.en: English used journal for a daily paper.
items.cn: 英语用 journal 指日报。

items.en: The -ist ending marked the person who wrote for it.
items.cn: -ist 词尾标出为它写作的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journ- stem; the near-meaning group holds news jobs by medium.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journ- 词干；近义组按媒介区分新闻行当。

entries.definition: The work or industry of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「新闻业」，同词干。

entries.definition: A trip from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「旅程」，同「日」词根。

entries.definition: Typical of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「新闻式的」，同词干。

entries.definition: One who gathers and reports news.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「记者」，偏出镜与现场。

entries.definition: A reporter based in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「驻外记者」，强调常驻。

entries.definition: One who prepares and approves copy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「编辑」，对稿件加工。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the day in the middle of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「日」留在词的正中间。

normal.en: French jour means day.
normal.cn: 法语 jour 就是「日」。

normal.en: A journal is a book written by the day.
normal.cn: journal 是逐日写下的本子。

normal.en: A journalist writes for the daily.
normal.cn: journalist 就是给日报写东西的人。

normal.en: -ist marks the person, -ism marks the trade.
normal.cn: -ist 指人，-ism 指这一行。

normal.en: Journalism is what the journalist does.
normal.cn: journalism 是 journalist 所做的事。

abstract.en: A journalist is a witness who files copy.
abstract.cn: 记者是交稿的目击者。

abstract.en: The day is the unit; the story is the product.
abstract.cn: 单位是日，产品是故事。

abstract.en: A good reporter asks boring questions until something breaks.
abstract.cn: 好记者一直问无聊的问题，直到有东西裂开。

examples.en: The journalist spent a week on the same street.
examples.cn: 这位记者在同一条街上待了一周。

examples.en: Two journalists were refused entry to the meeting.
examples.cn: 两名记者被拒绝进入会场。

examples.en: She moved from local radio to print journalism.
examples.cn: 她当地电台转做纸质新闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: journal（日报）+ ist（人）——给日报写字的人

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnalis「每日的」→ 古法语 journal「每日记录」→ 英语 journal + -ist → journalist。同族有 journalism、journalistic、journey。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: a news reporter, and a writer of longer pieces or columns.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：采写新闻的记者，以及撰写长文或专栏的撰稿人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone standing at the front of a crowd, asking and writing.
core.cn: 核心意象：挤在人群最前面、边问边写的人。

branches.en: THE NOTEBOOK: notes taken in the street.
branches.cn: 本子这条线：在街上记下的字。

branches.en: THE COLUMN: longer pieces written at a desk.
branches.cn: 专栏这条线：在书桌前写成的长文。

branches.en: THE DEADLINE: both senses live by the daily clock.
branches.cn: 截稿这条线：两个义项都跟着日内的钟走。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: both senses depend on someone who talked.
branches.cn: 消息源这条线：两个义项都要有人开口。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: writing is measured in days, not hours.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：写稿是按天算，不按小时算。

intro.en: Journalist is journ- "day" plus -al and the person-ending -ist.
intro.cn: journalist 是 journ-「日」加 -al，再加指人的 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Latin dies and diurnalis are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dies 与 diurnalis 均有记载。

items.example: The root also appears in journey.
It forms journal, a daily book.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 journal，每日的本子。

items.example: A near synonym with a Latin source.

definition_zh: 旅程；行程；历程
definition_en: an act of travelling from one place to another, especially a long one, or a long process of change
core_image: 一条从地平线开头、一直延伸到看不见尽头的路
scene: 清早的车站，人提着行李站在站台尽头，列车的灯从远处亮起来。The journey takes nine hours if the trains run on time.
sceneCN: 这里 journey 是「旅程」（第 1 个义项：从此地到彼地的行程），句意为如果列车准点，这趟要九个钟头。画面里的物件：行李、站台、列车灯。

pos.zh: 名词：旅程；行程；历程

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「旅行者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「旅行」
同源于 jour「日」的形近词，义为「日记；期刊」

senses.title: Travel from one place to another
senses.definition: an act of travelling, especially over a long distance
senses.definitionCN: 一次旅行，尤指长距离的
senses.example: The journey across the mountains took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 翻山那一趟走了三天。
senses.why: The basic sense is simply travel between two named places.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的义项就是两个地名之间的一趟走动。

senses.title: The distance travelled
senses.definition: the length of time or distance covered by travelling
senses.definitionCN: 旅行所花的时间或所走的路程
senses.example: It is a two-hour journey by bus.
senses.exampleCN: 坐公交要两个钟头的路程。
senses.why: The same word names the length of the trip, not only the trip itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指这趟路的长度，而不只是这趟出行。

senses.title: A process of change
senses.definition: a long personal or collective process of growth or change
senses.definitionCN: 个人或集体长期成长与改变的历程
senses.example: Learning the language was a journey of small victories.
senses.exampleCN: 学这门语言是一段由许多小胜利组成的历程。
senses.why: Modern English extended the road image to any long process of change.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把「路」的意象扩展到任何长期的改变过程。

intro.en: Journey began as French journée, "a day", because travel was measured in days.
intro.cn: journey 起初是法语 journée「一天」，因为旅程是按天来算的。

items.en: diurnus meant "of the day", from dies, "day".
items.cn: diurnus 意为「一天的」，来自 dies「日」。

items.en: journee meant "a day's work or a day's travel".
items.cn: journee 意为「一天的活儿或一天的行程」。

items.en: English took it as journee, still meaning a day's travel.
items.cn: 英语借作 journee，仍指一天的行程。

items.en: The meaning widened from one day to any trip.
items.cn: 词义从「一天」扩到「任何一趟行程」。

items.en: Modern usage adds the inner sense of a process of change.
items.cn: 现代用法又添了「内在历程」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journ- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for travelling.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journ- 词干；近义组收表示旅行的词。

entries.definition: A daily record or a magazine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「日记；期刊」，同词干。

entries.definition: A skilled worker paid by the day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「熟练工」，原文为按日计酬。

entries.definition: A person who writes for the news.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「记者」，同词干。

entries.definition: A short journey for pleasure or business.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「一趟」，多指短程。

entries.definition: A long journey by sea or space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「航行」，多指海上或太空。

entries.definition: A journey visiting several places.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「游览」，多点巡回。

normalIntro.en: These hooks measure the word in days, as the French did.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子像法国人那样，用「天」来量这个词。

normal.en: jour means day in French.
normal.cn: jour 在法语里是「白天」。

normal.en: A journey was once just a day of travel.
normal.cn: journey 原本只是一天的行程。

normal.en: Longer trips needed more jours, so the meaning grew.
normal.cn: 更长的路要更多「日」，词义就扩大了。

normal.en: A journal is what you write at the end of the day.
normal.cn: journal 是一天结束时写下的东西。

normal.en: Learning is a journey without a station.
normal.cn: 学习是一趟没有站台的旅程。

abstract.en: A journey is a straight line bent by weather.
abstract.cn: 旅程是一条被天气弄弯的直线。

abstract.en: The road is measured in days, the change in years.
abstract.cn: 路用天来量，改变用年来量。

abstract.en: Some journeys end where the traveller begins.
abstract.cn: 有些旅程的终点，正是出发时的自己。

examples.en: The journey from the coast to the capital takes a whole day.
examples.cn: 从海边到首都这一趟要一整天。

examples.en: She kept a notebook of every journey she took.
examples.cn: 她每一趟出行都记在一个本子上。

examples.en: His journey from factory worker to teacher took ten years.
examples.cn: 他从工人到教师的这条路走了十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: jour（日）+ ney —— 一段按日子数的路

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnus「一日的」→ 古法语 journee「一天的行程」→ 中古英语 journee → 现代英语 journey。同族有 journal、journeyman、journalist。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: travelling somewhere, the distance covered, and a long inner process.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：出门远行、所走的路程，以及长期的成长历程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road starting at the horizon and going out of sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从地平线起、伸到看不见尽头的路。

branches.en: THE PLATFORM: bags waiting for the departure.
branches.cn: 站台这条线：等着出发的行李。

branches.en: THE MILEAGE: the hours and miles the trip costs.
branches.cn: 里程这条线：这一趟花掉的时间与里数。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: an inner road from one self to another.
branches.cn: 改变这条线：从旧的自己走到新的自己。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: both senses count the trip in time.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：两个义项都用时间来数一趟路。

branches.en: THE PATIENCE: distance and growth both take days.
branches.cn: 耐心这条线：路程与成长都要一天一天来。

intro.en: Journey is borrowed from French with its day-root jour- intact.
intro.cn: journey 从法语整词借来，含「日」的词根 jour- 完好保留。

latinIntro.en: Latin dies and diurnus stand behind the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dies 与 diurnus 藏在法语词背后。

items.example: The root also appears in journal.

items.exampleCN: 它标出「一整天」这段长度。
英语把 journee 改成 journey。
同一个月「日」的词根，写了下来。

definition_zh: 判断力；看法；判决；天谴
definition_en: the ability to form sound opinions, an opinion so formed, or a formal ruling by a court
core_image: 天平上的砝码落下，指针抖了一下，停住
scene: 评审室里，三位评委听完演奏，各自在纸上写下分数。Her judgment of the young pianist was kinder than the others'.
sceneCN: 这里 judgment 指「经思考形成的评价」（第 1 个义项：形成稳妥看法的能力及其结果）；句意为她对那位年轻钢琴家的评价比其他人宽厚。场景要素：评分纸、铅笔、舞台监听音箱。

pos.zh: 判断力；看法；判决；天谴

derivatives.zh: 与 judgment 同出拉丁语中「法官」一词，指审理者或审理这一行为
由拉丁语「法庭的」一词进入英语，指与司法有关的
由 judge 加形容词后缀构成，指有见地的、审慎的
由 judgmental 加副词后缀构成，指以评判的姿态；属另一条形容词线
由表「在前」的前缀加「判断」的拉丁词构成，指预先形成的判断，后指偏见

senses.title: The ability to form sound opinions
senses.definition: the capacity to weigh evidence and reach a sensible conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 权衡证据并得出合宜结论的能力
senses.example: Years of editing gave her a reliable judgment about which submissions would sell.
senses.exampleCN: 多年编辑经验让她对哪些投稿卖得动有可靠的判断。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it joins law and speaking, so judging originally meant declaring what is right, and the mental capacity sense grew from that authority.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁词把法律与言说连在一起，因此「判断」原指宣示何为正当，心智能力义由此权威感生长出来。

senses.title: An opinion reached
senses.definition: a conclusion one has come to about a person, work or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对人、作品或情形得出的结论
senses.example: My judgment is that the proposal is sound but the timing is wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 我的看法是方案本身可靠，但时机不对。
senses.why: Once the capacity produces something, the same noun names the product, which is why it appears with possessives.
senses.whyCN: 能力一旦产出结果，同一个名词就指那个结果，因此它常带所有格。

senses.title: A ruling by a court
senses.definition: the formal decision of a court that settles the rights of the parties
senses.definitionCN: 法院了结各方权利义务的正式决定
senses.example: The judgment ordered the company to restore the wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 判决责令该公司恢复这片湿地。
senses.why: Law was the earliest home of the word, and the courtroom sense never faded even as the everyday sense broadened.
senses.whyCN: 法律是这个词最早的家，即便日常义后来拓宽，法庭义也从未消退。

senses.title: A formal decision of a tribunal
senses.definition: an award or finding issued by a panel, arbitrator or competition jury
senses.definitionCN: 由评审团、仲裁人或竞赛评委作出的裁定或评定
senses.example: The arbitration judgment awarded costs to the smaller firm.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁裁决把费用判给了那家较小的公司。
senses.why: Any body that must settle a dispute borrows the courtroom noun, so the sense travels from courts to arbitrators and juries.
senses.whyCN: 任何必须了结争议的机构都会借用这个法庭名词，于是这一义从法院延伸到仲裁人与评委。

senses.title: The exercise of judicial authority
senses.definition: the act of deciding as one lawfully entitled to decide, as in the phrase to sit in judgment
senses.definitionCN: 以合法资格作出裁断的行为，如「坐在审判席上」这一说法
senses.example: The commission sits in judgment on complaints about broadcasters.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会对针对广播机构的投诉行使裁断权。
senses.why: The noun can name not just the ruling but the authority being exercised, which is why it survives in formal legal phrasing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词不只指裁决，也指被行使的权威，因此它在正式法律措辞中留存。

senses.title: Divine judgment
senses.definition: in religious language, the verdict of a higher power on human conduct
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语言中，更高力量对人类行为的裁决
senses.example: The sermon warned of judgment and of mercy in the same breath.
senses.exampleCN: 布道在同一口气里既警告审判，也提到怜悯。
senses.why: Religious language took the courtroom image and moved the judge upward, so the word acquired a sense no human court can supply.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言借走法庭意象，把审判者移到天上，这个词于是获得人间法庭给不了的义项。

senses.title: Critical evaluation in a field
senses.definition: the trained assessment of quality in a craft, as in editorial or artistic judgment
senses.definitionCN: 对某一行业或艺术品质的专业评估
senses.example: The curator's judgment on the drawings was trusted by three museums.
senses.exampleCN: 这位策展人对这批素描的品评得到三家博物馆信赖。
senses.why: Where a field has standards but no rules, practitioners rely on trained judgment, and the word names that reliance.
senses.whyCN: 当一个领域有标准却无规则时，从业者依赖训练出的判断，这个词就指这种依赖。

senses.title: A judgment call
senses.definition: a decision that must rest on opinion because the rules and data leave the case open
senses.definitionCN: 规则与数据都未定论、只能凭看法作出的决定
senses.example: Whether to publish before the holiday was a judgment call.
senses.exampleCN: 要不要在假期前发表，是个只能凭判断的决定。
senses.why: The fixed phrase marks the point where calculation stops and opinion must act, which is the everyday survival of the old authority sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个固定说法标出计算终止、看法必须上场的那一刻，也是古老权威义在日常中的遗留。

intro.en: Judgment comes through Old French from Latin judicium, built on judex 'judge', which joins jus 'law, right' to dicere 'to say, declare'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: judgment 经古法语来自拉丁语 judicium，其基础是 judex「法官」，由 jus「法律、权利」与 dicere「说、宣告」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Jus meant 'law, right, justice'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to the verb for swearing an oath is a hypothesis.
items.cn: jus 意为「法律、权利、正义」。其更早来源未得到证明；有人提出它与表「发誓」的动词有关，那只是假说。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, declare'. The same verb builds dictate, predict and verdict.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、宣告」。同一个动词还构成 dictate、predict 与 verdict。

items.en: Jus plus dicere produced judex 'one who declares the law', hence the judge.
items.cn: jus 加 dicere 构成 judex「宣告法律的人」，即法官。

items.en: The noun judicium named the declaring of a right, then the ruling itself and the faculty of ruling well.
items.cn: 名词 judicium 既指宣告权利，也指裁决本身，以及善于裁断的能力。

items.en: Old French jugement carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, where legal use came first and general use followed.
items.cn: 古法语 jugement 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，法律用法先行，一般用法随后。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is recorded only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of jus is unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早的英语用例只有约略记载；jus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that are routinely mixed up with judgment; group two holds near neighbours for an opinion or a ruling.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，常与本词张冠李戴；第二组是表示看法或裁定的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun for the official and the verb for what that official does; judgment is the ruling or the capacity, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 作名词指法官，作动词指法官所做的事；judgment 指裁决或能力，不指人。

entries.definition: An adjective for the court system and its procedures, not for a person's opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容法院系统及其程序，而非个人的看法。

entries.definition: Built to mean full of good judgment, so it is a compliment; it is not the adjective of judgmental.
entries.definitionCN: 构成上意为「富于良好判断」，因此是褒义；它并不是 judgmental 的形容词原形。

entries.definition: Built with the prefix meaning 'before' plus the same judging root, so it literally means a judgment formed in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「在前」的前缀加同一个「判断」词根构成，字面就是「事先形成的判断」。

entries.definition: The formal finding of a jury, literally a true saying; it is the courtroom sense of judgment made specific.
entries.definitionCN: 指陪审团的正式认定，字面是「如实说出」，是法院义的具体化。

entries.definition: A view held without the weight of authority; judgment suggests that the view was earned by weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 指所持的看法，不带权威分量；judgment 暗示这看法是权衡得来的。

entries.definition: The process or result of measuring something against criteria; judgment adds the personal act of deciding.
entries.definitionCN: 指按标准衡量的过程或结果；judgment 多了「人作出裁断」这一层。

entries.definition: The ability to see subtle differences, especially in quality; judgment stresses the conclusion rather than the seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 指看出细微差别的能力，尤其在品质上；judgment 强调结论而非看见。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、真实的词族与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: The Latin noun joins law and declaring, so judgment is law spoken out loud.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁名词把「法律」与「宣告」连在一起，因此判断就是被说出来的法。

normal.en: The family runs judge, judgment, judicial, judicious, judiciary, prejudice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 judge、judgment、judicial、judicious、judiciary、prejudice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the courtroom origin: pass judgment, sit in judgment, a court judgment.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出法庭出身：作出评判、坐在审判席上、法院判决。

normal.en: The everyday phrase a judgment call marks the point where rules run out.
normal.cn: 日常说法「凭判断的决定」标出规则用尽的那一刻。

normal.en: British writing often spells the noun judgement, while American writing prefers judgment.
normal.cn: 英式写作常拼作 judgement，美式写作多用 judgment。

abstract.en: Picture a balance whose pointer stops only after the weights are all placed.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，砝码全部放好之后指针才停住。

abstract.en: Picture a gavel that falls once and ends every argument in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一把法槌落下一次，房间里所有争论就此结束。

abstract.en: Picture a critic who looks at a painting for a long time before saying a single word.
abstract.cn: 想象一位评论家看画很久，才说出一句话。

examples.en: The recruiter trusted her judgment more than the test scores.
examples.cn: 招聘者更信她的判断，而不是那些测验分数。

examples.en: The court issued a judgment that reopened the old case.
examples.cn: 法院作出判决，让这桩旧案重新开庭。

examples.en: Whether to speak now or wait was a judgment call.
examples.cn: 现在开口还是再等等，是个只能凭判断的决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「judge 法官 + ment 行为」——法官作出的，就是判决与判断

root: 拉丁 judicium「裁断」= judex「法官」+ 名词后缀；judex 又由 jus「法律、权利」与 dicere「说、宣告」构成；jus 更深来源不确定。英语 judgment。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of declaring what is right: a capacity, an opinion, a court's ruling, an arbitrator's award, the authority behind it, a heavenly verdict, a craft's evaluation and a call made where rules stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：宣告何为正当。它依次是能力、看法、法院判决、仲裁裁定、背后的权威、天上的裁决、行业内的品评，以及规则用尽处凭看法作出的决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance whose pointer trembles and then stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上的指针抖了一下，然后停住。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND PRODUCT: the ability to weigh and the opinion it produces are the same act seen inside and outside.
branches.cn: 能力与产物：权衡的能力与它产出的看法，是同一动作的内外两面。

branches.en: COURT AND AUTHORITY: a ruling and the lawful power to issue it are inseparable in legal use.
branches.cn: 判决与权威：在法律用法里，裁决与作出裁决的合法权力不可分。

branches.en: BORROWED COURTROOM: arbitrators and juries use the noun because they too must end a dispute.
branches.cn: 借来的法庭：仲裁人与评委也用这个名词，因为他们同样必须了结争议。

branches.en: UPWARD VERDICT: religion moves the judge above the room, adding a sense no human court supplies.
branches.cn: 向上的裁决：宗教把审判者移到房间之上，增添了人间法庭给不了的义项。

branches.en: TRAINED AND OPEN CASES: professional evaluation and the judgment call both act where written rules fall silent.
branches.cn: 专业与开放情形：行业品评与凭判断的决定，都在明文规则沉默处发挥作用。

intro.en: Judgment is two Latin pieces plus a Latin noun suffix, and the pieces also build the rest of the legal family.
intro.cn: judgment 由两个拉丁成分加一个拉丁名词后缀构成，这些成分还构成整个法律词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin jus gives justice, jurist and jury; Latin dicere gives dictate, predict, verdict and the same ending in prejudice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 jus 衍生 justice、jurist 与 jury；拉丁 dicere 衍生 dictate、predict、verdict，以及 prejudice 中的同一成分。

items.example: The root supplies the legal half of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供词义中「法」的那一半。

items.example: The root supplies the speaking that makes a ruling official.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供使裁决成为正式的那种言说。

items.example: The compound produced the name of the official.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词造出了官员的名称。

items.example: The noun is the base that French and English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是法语与英语借用的基础。

items.example: The suffix marks the ruling as something produced and recorded.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把裁决标为被产出、被记录之物。

items.meaning: a ruling or a formed opinion
items.example: English keeps one noun for the act, the result and the capacity.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一个名词指行为、结果与能力。

items.example: The person noun survives beside the abstract one.
items.exampleCN: 指人的名词与抽象名词并存。

items.example: The adjective stays inside the legal sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词留在法律义之内。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun of office into an adjective of system.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把职务名词变成制度形容词。

definition_zh: 丛林；密林；混乱拥挤之处
definition_en: a thick tropical forest full of tangled plants, or any place that feels crowded and without rules
core_image: 藤蔓从地面爬到树冠，脚下连一步平地都找不到
scene: 雨还没停，树叶上滴着水，道路在十米之外就完全消失了。The path vanished into the jungle after the first bend.
sceneCN: 这里 jungle 是「丛林」（第 1 个义项：热带浓密树林），句意为路拐过第一个弯就消失在丛林里。画面里的物件：藤蔓、树冠、积水。

pos.zh: 名词：丛林；密林；混乱竞争之地

collocations.phrase: cut a path through the jungle

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「丛林般的」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「被丛林覆盖的」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「长满丛林的」

senses.title: Thick tropical forest
senses.definition: a forest in a hot wet region where plants grow so thickly that movement is hard
senses.definitionCN: 炎热潮湿地区树木藤蔓密到难以行走的森林
senses.example: Tigers still live in these jungles.
senses.exampleCN: 这些丛林里仍有老虎生活。
senses.why: The geographic sense is the one the word was borrowed for.
senses.whyCN: 地理义正是这个词被借进英语时所指的。

senses.title: A wild, crowded place
senses.definition: a place or situation that feels crowded, lawless, and hard to survive
senses.definitionCN: 拥挤、缺少规则、难以生存的地方或处境
senses.example: The market at noon is a jungle of carts and shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 中午的市场是一片推车与叫喊的丛林。
senses.why: The metaphor uses the forest to talk about crowded, ruleless human places.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借森林来说拥挤、少规则的人间场所。

senses.title: A mess of things
senses.definition: a confused mass of objects or words
senses.definitionCN: 一堆纠缠不清的物件或文字
senses.example: The report is a jungle of numbers and abbreviations.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是一团数字与缩写的丛林。
senses.why: The mess sense is the metaphor pushed toward pure confusion.
senses.whyCN: 「杂乱」义是这个比喻推到纯粹的混乱那一端。

intro.en: Jungle came from Hindi jangal, "waste land, forest", which goes back to Sanskrit jangala, "dry ground".
intro.cn: jungle 来自印地语 jangal「荒地、森林」，更早是梵语 jangala「干燥之地」。

items.en: jangala meant "dry, arid land".
items.cn: jangala 意为「干燥荒芜之地」。

items.en: jangal named waste or uncultivated land, often wooded.
items.cn: jangal 指荒废未耕种之地，常长着树。

items.en: English in India used jungle for dense Indian forest.
items.cn: 在印度的英国人用 jungle 指印度浓密森林。

items.en: The word entered general English in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词在十九世纪进入普通英语。

items.en: Kipling and later writing fixed the tropical image.
items.cn: 吉卜林及其后的作品固定了热带丛林的意象。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the jun-/jung- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for dense wild growth.
note.cn: 形近组共用 jun-/jung- 开头；近义组收表示浓密野生植被的词。

entries.definition: Like a jungle, thick and wild.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「丛林般的」，同族词。

entries.definition: A confused mixture of things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「杂乱的一堆」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A harsh ringing of metal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「刺耳声响」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A dense tropical forest with heavy rain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「雨林」，偏地理。

entries.definition: Land untouched by people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「荒野」，无人居住。

entries.definition: A mass of bushes growing close together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「灌木丛」，规模较小。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the word back from tropical film scenes to a Sanskrit adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它从热带电影画面追到梵语形容词。

normal.en: Hindi jangal meant waste or wooded land.
normal.cn: 印地语 jangal 指荒地或有树林的地。

normal.en: Sanskrit jangala meant dry ground.
normal.cn: 梵语 jangala 意为干燥之地。

normal.en: Dry land became wet forest in the English image.
normal.cn: 干燥之地在英语的意象里成了潮湿森林。

normal.en: Jungle law is survival without rules.
normal.cn: jungle law 就是没有规则的生存。

normal.en: A concrete jungle has trees of steel.
normal.cn: 水泥丛林里长的是钢铁做的树。

abstract.en: A jungle is a forest that says no to roads.
abstract.cn: 丛林是一片对道路说不的森林。

abstract.en: Where the vines meet, the ground disappears.
abstract.cn: 藤蔓相接的地方，地面就消失了。

abstract.en: Every crowded market is a small jungle.
abstract.cn: 每个拥挤的市场都是一小片丛林。

examples.en: The village sits at the edge of a thick jungle.
examples.cn: 这个村子坐落在浓密丛林的边上。

examples.en: New staff soon learn the jungle of office politics.
examples.cn: 新员工很快就摸清了办公室政治的丛林。

examples.en: The notebook was a jungle of arrows and odd words.
examples.cn: 那本笔记是一团箭头和怪词组成的丛林。

dict_mnemonic.text: jangal（印地语「荒地、树林」）—— 密到走不动的森林

root: 梵语 jangala「干燥之地」→ 印地语 jangal「荒地；树林」→ 英印英语 jungle → 现代英语 jungle。同族有 jungly、jungled。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: tropical thick forest, a crowded lawless place, and a tangled mess.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：热带密林、拥挤无规则之地，以及杂乱的一团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vines climbing from soil to canopy with no flat ground left.
core.cn: 核心意象：藤蔓从地面爬到树冠，脚下没有平地。

branches.en: THE PATH: a route that vanishes after one bend.
branches.cn: 小径这条线：拐过一个弯就消失的路。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a crowd where rules seem absent.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：规则像是缺席的人群。

branches.en: THE REPORT: numbers and arrows tangled together.
branches.cn: 报告这条线：数字与箭头缠成一团。

branches.en: THE SURVIVAL: both senses test who can keep going.
branches.cn: 生存这条线：两个义项都在考验谁能走下去。

branches.en: THE MESS: crowding and tangling are the same picture.
branches.cn: 杂乱这条线：拥挤与纠缠是同一幅画。

intro.en: Jungle is borrowed from Hindi as a whole; only English endings are added.
intro.cn: jungle 是从印地语整体借来的，只有后面加的英语词尾属于英语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word is Indic, so latinEntries stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源，是印度语系词，所以 latinEntries 留空。

items.exampleCN: 英语写作 jungle，而非 jangal。

items.example: It forms jungled, covered with jungle.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jungled，被丛林覆盖的。

items.example: It forms jungle cat and jungle law.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jungle cat 与 jungle law。

items.example: A look-alike with a different origin.

definition_zh: 陪审团；评判委员会；评奖团
definition_en: a group of ordinary people chosen to listen to a case and decide it, or a group that decides a competition
core_image: 十二个人坐在木栏后面，低头听完双方发言再做结论
scene: 法庭里空气很闷，旁听席坐满了人，栏杆后那一组人一直在记笔记。The jury returned after four hours with a clear verdict.
sceneCN: 这里 jury 是「陪审团」（第 1 个义项：依法听审并裁决的一组普通公民），句意为陪审团四小时后回来，给出了明确的裁决。画面里的物件：法庭、木栏、笔记本。

pos.zh: 名词：陪审团；评判委员会；评奖团（集合用法）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 jur- 加 -or 构成，指陪审员
由 jur- 加 -ist 构成，指法学家
由 jur- 加 -idical 构成，义为「司法上的」
由 jur- 加 dictio 构成，义为「司法管辖权」

senses.title: A body deciding a court case
senses.definition: a group of citizens sworn to hear evidence and give a verdict in a court
senses.definitionCN: 依法宣誓听取证据并在法庭上作出裁决的一组公民
senses.example: The jury took two days to reach a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团用了两天得出结论。
senses.why: The core sense is a sworn body that speaks a verdict for the court.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是向法庭宣告裁决的一个宣誓团体。

senses.title: A panel judging a competition
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to judge a contest and choose winners
senses.definitionCN: 被选出为一比评优劣、决定获奖者的一组人
senses.example: The jury gave the prize to an unknown filmmaker.
senses.exampleCN: 评委会把奖给了一位无名导演。
senses.why: A contest panel judges the way a court does: it weighs and decides.
senses.whyCN: 比赛的评委与法庭一样评判：称量然后决定。

senses.title: Members collectively, with plural agreement
senses.definition: the group treated as a plural body in grammar, so the jury can be said to disagree
senses.definitionCN: 语法上按复数处理，因此可说陪审团意见不一致
senses.example: The jury were still arguing at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 到九点陪审团还在争论。
senses.why: British grammar lets a collective noun take a plural verb when the members act apart.
senses.whyCN: 英式语法允许集合名词在成员各自行动时接复数动词。

senses.title: A temporary makeshift device
senses.definition: a temporary arrangement in nautical or technical use, as a makeshift mast
senses.definitionCN: 航海或技术语境中的临时凑合装置，如临时桅杆
senses.example: They rigged a jury rudder after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后他们装了一副临时舵。
senses.why: Sailors use the word for a thing thrown together to meet an emergency.
senses.whyCN: 水手用这个词指为应付紧急情况匆匆凑成的东西。

senses.title: A body of citizens summoned by law
senses.definition: the body of citizens summoned to serve, seen as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 被依法召集服役的公民群体，作为制度看待
senses.example: Jury service is a duty of the citizen.
senses.exampleCN: 担任陪审员是公民的义务。
senses.why: The institution side names not a case but the standing role of citizens in law.
senses.whyCN: 制度这一面指的不是某个案子，而是公民在法律中的常设角色。

intro.en: Jury comes from Old French juree, an oath, from Latin jurare, to swear, and shares the root jus, law.
intro.cn: jury 来自古法语 juree「誓言」，源自拉丁语 jurare「宣誓」，与 jus「法」同根。

items.en: jurare meant to swear an oath, and jus meant law or right.
items.cn: jurare 意为宣誓，jus 意为法或权利。

items.en: juree named a sworn body of men or the oath they took.
items.cn: juree 指宣誓组成的一群人，或他们所立的誓言。

items.en: English borrowed jury in the fourteenth century as the sworn body in a court.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 jury，指法庭上的宣誓团体。

items.en: The competition sense developed much later, as prizes became contests.
items.cn: 比赛评委义很晚才出现，源于评奖变成竞赛。

items.en: The nautical jury sense is separate and probably from a different source.

senses.title: Fairness as a quality
senses.definition: the quality of being fair and giving each person what is due

senses.title: The system of courts

senses.title: A fair outcome for someone

senses.exampleCN: 这些家庭终于在法庭上得到了公正。

senses.title: Fair treatment in presentation

senses.whyCN: 量得准确的一次判断，就是缩小的正义。

definition_zh: 正当理由；辩护；辩解；（神学）称义；（排版）两端对齐
definition_en: the act of showing that something is right or reasonable; a reason given in defence; (theology) the state of being made righteous; (printing) the alignment of text to both margins
core_image: 天平两端分别放上指控与证据，指针最终停在水平位置

senses.title: Showing something to be reasonable
senses.definition: the act of demonstrating that a decision, claim, or action is right or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 证明某个决定、主张或行为正确或合理的行为
senses.example: The report offers a strong justification for raising the minimum wage.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告为提高最低工资提供了有力理由。
senses.why: Justification is justify + -ation. Justify comes from Late Latin justificare, justus 'just' + facere 'to make': to make something just, or to show that it already is. The suffix names the act of making that showing.
senses.whyCN: justification 是 justify + -ation。justify 源自晚期拉丁语 justificare，即 justus“公正”+ facere“使”：使某事成为公正的，或表明它本就公正。后缀命名的是这一“表明”的行为。

senses.title: A defence offered for conduct
senses.definition: a reason put forward to defend an action that others may criticise
senses.definitionCN: 为他人可能批评的行为提出的辩护理由
senses.example: His justification for leaving early was that the trains had stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 他早退的理由是列车已经停运。
senses.why: This sense is personal and often defensive: the justification is offered after the act, to answer a challenge. The word assumes a critic exists, which is why it often sounds like an argument rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是个人化的，常带防御性：理由在行为之后提出，用来回应质疑。这个词预设有一个批评者存在，所以它常听起来像论辩而非证明。

senses.title: Justification in theology
senses.definition: the act by which God is said to make a sinner righteous, central to Reformation disputes
senses.definitionCN: 上帝使罪人成为义人的行为，是宗教改革争论的核心
senses.example: Luther taught justification by faith alone.
senses.exampleCN: 路德教导“唯独因信称义”。
senses.why: Theology uses the word in its strongest sense: not a claim that someone is just, but a change that makes them so. The Latin facere 'make' is doing real work here, unlike in the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 神学用这个词的最强意义：不是声称某人公正，而是使其成为公正的改变。这里拉丁语 facere“使”真正起作用，与日常义不同。

senses.title: Legal or official grounds
senses.definition: the legal grounds that make an action permissible or a claim admissible
senses.definitionCN: 使某行为被允许或某主张可被接受的法律依据
senses.example: The court found no legal justification for the search.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定这次搜查没有法律依据。
senses.why: Law asks not whether an action was reasonable in general but whether it was authorised. Justification here is a formal finding that the required grounds existed.
senses.whyCN: 法律不问行为在一般意义上是否合理，而问它是否被授权。这里的 justification 是对“所需依据确实存在”的正式认定。

senses.title: Text alignment in printing
senses.definition: the adjustment of spacing so that lines of text align evenly at the margin
senses.definitionCN: 调整字距，使各行文字在页边对齐
senses.example: Full justification stretched the words across the narrow column.
senses.exampleCN: 两端对齐把字距拉宽以填满窄栏。
senses.why: This sense comes from the same Latin root by a different path: to justify a line is to make its edges 'just' or exact. The printing trade borrowed the moral word and gave it a mechanical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自同一拉丁词根但路径不同：让一行文字的边缘“正”或精确。印刷业借用了这个道德词，赋予它机械含义。

senses.title: Epistemic justification
senses.definition: the reason or warrant that makes a belief reasonable to hold
senses.definitionCN: 使某个信念有理由被持有的依据或保证
senses.example: Philosophers distinguish justification from mere belief.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家把证成与单纯的相信区分开来。
senses.why: Philosophy asks what makes a belief acceptable rather than merely held. Justification here is the warrant, and the debates are about whether it must be internal, external, or both.
senses.whyCN: 哲学追问是什么使一个信念可被接受，而不只是被持有。这里的 justification 是保证，争论在于它必须是内在的、外在的，还是两者兼有。

senses.title: Grounds in an argument
senses.definition: the premises or evidence that support a conclusion in reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 推理中支持结论的前提或证据
senses.example: The justification for the inference lies in the correlation itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这一推断的依据就在相关性本身。
senses.why: Logic needs a word for the support relation between premises and conclusion. Justification names that relation, not the psychological confidence of the person reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要一个词来指前提与结论之间的支持关系。justification 命名这一关系，而不是推理者的心理确信。

senses.title: Business case for a request
senses.definition: a written case showing why a purchase, project, or budget is worth approving
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项采购、项目或预算值得批准的书面论证
senses.example: The manager attached a two-page justification to the purchase order.
senses.exampleCN: 经理在采购单后附了两页理由说明。
senses.why: Organizations require justification to make decisions auditable: someone must show that the cost buys a benefit. The word turns a preference into a record.
senses.whyCN: 组织要求理由说明，是为了让决策可被审计：必须有人证明这笔成本换来了收益。这个词把偏好变成记录。

intro.en: Justification is justify + -ation. Justify comes from Late Latin justificare, from justus 'just, lawful' and facere 'to make'. Justus itself goes back to ius 'law, right', the same root that gives justice, judge, and jury.
intro.cn: justification 是 justify + -ation。justify 源自晚期拉丁语 justificare，由 justus“公正、合法”与 facere“使”构成。justus 本身上溯 ius“法、权利”，同一词根还给出 justice、judge 与 jury。

items.en: Latin ius (genitive iuris) meant 'law, right, justice'. Justus 'lawful, just' came from it, and iudex 'judge' was literally ius + dicere 'say the law'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ius（属格 iuris）意为“法、权利、正义”。justus“合法的、公正的”由此而来，而 iudex“法官”字面是 ius + dicere“说出法律”。

items.en: Justificare combined justus with facere 'to make': to make someone or something just, or to show it as just. The noun justificatio named this making.
items.cn: justificare 把 justus 与 facere“使”结合：使某人或某物成为公正的，或表明其为公正。名词 justificatio 命名这一“使之”过程。

items.en: English justification entered through Old French in the fourteenth century. The word carried both the everyday sense 'defence' and the theological sense 'being made righteous'.
items.cn: 英语 justification 于 14 世纪经古法语进入。这个词同时带有日常义“辩护”与神学义“被称为义”。

items.en: The Reformation made justification a contested technical term: whether it is a change in the sinner or a verdict about them. The word's later legal and philosophical uses inherited this precision.
items.cn: 宗教改革使 justification 成为有争议的术语：它是罪人身上的改变，还是关于他的判决。这个词后来的法律与哲学用法继承了这种精确性。

items.en: The printing trade used 'justify' for making a line's edges exact, which produced the noun 'justification' in typography. The moral word acquired a mechanical sense.
items.cn: 印刷业用 justify 指把一行文字的边缘弄“正”，由此产生排版义 justification。这个道德词获得机械含义。

items.en: Analytic philosophy made justification a central term for the warrant of belief, while organizations made 'justification' a written business case. The word now covers proof, defence, and record.
items.cn: 分析哲学使 justification 成为信念保证的核心术语，组织则把 justification 变成书面商业论证。这个词如今覆盖证明、辩护与记录。

note.en: The look-alike group separates words built on ius 'law' or on other roots; the near-meaning group separates reason, defence, and excuse.
note.cn: 形近组区分建立在 ius“法”或其他词根上的词；近义组区分“理由”“辩护”与“借口”。

entries.tag: same ius root noun of rightness
entries.definition: fairness or the administration of law. It comes from Latin iustitia, from iustus, but names the virtue itself rather than the argument for a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 公平或司法。它来自拉丁语 iustitia，源自 iustus，但命名的是美德本身，而不是为某个决定作论证。

entries.definition: a decision or opinion. It comes from iudicium, built on ius + dicere 'say', so it names the verdict, not the grounds offered for it.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决或判断。它来自 iudicium，由 ius + dicere“说”构成，因此命名的是判决，而非为其提出的依据。

entries.definition: the checking of a fact or claim. It comes from verus 'true', and asks whether something is factually correct rather than whether it is justified.
entries.definitionCN: 对事实或主张的核查。它来自 verus“真”，问的是某事在事实上是否正确，而不是它是否有正当理由。

entries.definition: a cause or explanation for something. It can be neutral or trivial, while justification implies that the reason is adequate to defend the act.
entries.definitionCN: 某事的原因或解释。它可以是中性或琐碎的，而 justification 暗示该理由足以为此行为辩护。

entries.definition: an argument or action that protects against criticism. Justification is the content of such a defence: the grounds that make it work.
entries.definitionCN: 为抵御批评而提出的论证或行动。justification 是这种辩护的内容：使它成立的那些依据。

entries.definition: a reason offered to avoid blame, often not accepted by the hearer. It is weaker than justification, which claims genuine adequacy.
entries.definitionCN: 为逃避责备而给的理由，常不被听者接受。它比 justification 弱，后者声称确实充分。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: ius 'law' + facere 'make', the theological phrase justification by faith, and the typographic use of justified text.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：ius“法”+ facere“使”、神学说法 justification by faith，以及排版中的 justified text。

normal.en: justus means 'lawful' and facere means 'make': justification is making a case stand as right.
normal.cn: justus 意为“合法的”，facere 意为“使”：justification 就是让一个说法站得住、显得正当。

normal.en: justice, judge, jury, and justification all descend from ius, the Latin word for law.
normal.cn: justice、judge、jury、justification 都源自 ius，即拉丁语“法”。

normal.en: In theology the word is strongest: it makes a person righteous, not merely calls them so.
normal.cn: 在神学里这个词最强：它使人成为义人，而不只是称他为义人。

normal.en: In printing, to justify a line is to make its edges exact — 'just' in the geometric sense.
normal.cn: 在印刷中，justify a line 是把行边弄“正”——几何意义上的“正”。

normal.en: A purchase order needs a justification so that the spending can be audited later.
normal.cn: 采购单需要理由说明，好让这笔支出日后可被审计。

abstract.en: The word always answers a challenge: it exists because someone might say 'no' or 'why'.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是在回应质疑：它之所以存在，是因为有人可能说“不行”或“为什么”。

abstract.en: It claims adequacy, not truth — a justification can be sound and the decision still wrong.
abstract.cn: 它主张的是充分性，而不是真理性——理由可以成立，决定仍然可能是错的。

abstract.en: From courtroom to column width, the same idea recurs: making edges come out even.
abstract.cn: 从法庭到栏宽，同一个想法反复出现：让边缘变得齐整。

examples.en: There is no justification for treating one group differently.
examples.cn: 没有正当理由区别对待某个群体。

examples.en: The theologian wrote about justification by faith alone.
examples.cn: 这位神学家论述了“唯独因信称义”。

examples.en: The columns look tidy because the text is fully justified.
examples.cn: 因为文字采用了两端对齐，各栏看起来很整齐。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扎斯提飞开心”——把理由“扎”实、“提”出来，让人飞着也开心地接受 → justification 正当理由、辩护

root: 拉丁语 ius/iur-“法、权利”→ iustus“公正的”+ facere“使”+ -ation；字面义“使之公正、使之站得住”，核心是“为某决定提供充分依据”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of justification all answer the question 'why is this acceptable?': a decision, a conduct, a sinner, a search, a line of type, a belief, an inference, and a purchase. The word always offers grounds, and grounds can always be challenged.
sensesIntro.cn: justification 的八个义项都在回答“这为什么可以被接受？”：一个决定、一种行为、一个罪人、一次搜查、一行文字、一个信念、一次推断、一笔采购。这个词总是提供依据，而依据总是可以被质疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with accusation on one side and evidence on the other, settling level.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一端放指控、一端放证据，最终停在水平。

branches.en: EVERYDAY DEFENCE: a decision or an action is shown to be reasonable, often after criticism.
branches.cn: 日常辩护：决定或行为被表明合理，常在批评之后。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: theology and law decide whether the grounds actually transform or authorise.
branches.cn: 权威：神学与法律判定依据究竟能改变人，还是能授权行为。

branches.en: TYPOGRAPHY: the same word makes a line's edges exact.
branches.cn: 排版：同一个词让一行文字的边缘变得精确。

branches.en: REASONING: philosophy and logic ask what warrants a belief or an inference.
branches.cn: 推理：哲学与逻辑追问是什么为信念或推断提供保证。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: a written case turns a preference into an auditable record.
branches.cn: 管理：书面论证把偏好变成可审计的记录。

intro.en: Justification is justify + -ation, from Late Latin justificare (justus + facere). The family is divided between derivatives of justify and the ius 'law' relatives justice, just, judge, and jury.
intro.cn: justification 是 justify + -ation，源自晚期拉丁语 justificare（justus + facere）。家族分为 justify 的派生词与 ius“法”的亲属词 justice、just、judge、jury。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius (genitive iuris) 'law, right' produced iustus 'just', iustitia 'justice', iudex 'judge' (ius + dicere 'say'), and iudicium 'judgement'. Justificare is a Late Latin compound of iustus with facere 'make'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ius（属格 iuris）“法、权利”产生 iustus“公正的”、iustitia“正义”、iudex“法官”（ius + dicere“说”）、iudicium“判断”。justificare 是晚期拉丁语中 iustus 与 facere“使”的复合词。

items.meaning: grounds that show something is right; alignment
items.meaningCN: 正当理由；辩护；对齐（-ation 构成名词）
items.example: No justification was given for the delay.
items.exampleCN: 对这次延误没有给出理由。

items.meaning: to show to be right; to align text
items.meaningCN: 证明正当；为……辩护；对齐（源自晚期拉丁语）
items.example: How can you justify the expense?
items.exampleCN: 你如何证明这笔开支合理？

items.meaning: able to be defended as right
items.meaningCN: 有正当理由的（-able 表可能）
items.example: The delay was justifiable in the circumstances.
items.exampleCN: 在当时情况下，延误是有理由的。

items.meaningCN: 有理由地（-ly 构成副词）
没有正当理由的（un- 表否定）
辩护性的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 他加了一条辩解性脚注。

items.structure: Latin iudex, from ius + dicere 'say the law'

definition_zh: 证明……正当；为……辩护；使合理化；调整使排满（排版）
definition_en: to show that something is right or reasonable, or to give a good reason for it
core_image: 有人举起一张纸，一条一条向对面的人解释为什么这样做没错
scene: 会议室里被质问的一方把证据摊开，逐条说明当初的决定为什么合理。Nothing can justify that much expense on one dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 justify 是「证明……正当」（第 1 个义项：给出理由说明某事合理），句意为没有任何理由能为一顿晚饭花那么多钱开脱。画面里的物件：会议室、证据文件、对面的听众。

pos.zh: 动词：证明正当；为……辩解；使合理；（排版）使两端对齐

derivatives.zh: 由 justify 加 -cation 构成，义为「辩护；正当理由」
由 justify 加 -ed 构成，义为「有正当理由的」
由 justify 加 -able 构成，义为「可辩解的」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「无正当理由的」

senses.title: To show that something is right
senses.definition: to give reasons that show an action or claim is right or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 给出理由以证明某行为或主张合理
senses.example: How do you justify spending so much on a phone?
senses.exampleCN: 你凭什么为花这么多钱买手机找理由？
senses.why: The word sets a thing on the scale of right and asks whether it balances.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把一件事放上「正当」的秤，问它是否配平。

senses.title: To defend against criticism
senses.definition: to answer criticism by defending a choice or statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过辩护某个选择或说法来回应批评
senses.example: The manager justified his decision to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 经理向全队为自己的决定作了辩解。
senses.why: Justifying is talking back to an accusation with reasons.
senses.whyCN: 辩解就是用理由回应一项指责。

senses.title: To be a good reason for
senses.definition: to be the reason that makes something acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 本身构成使某事可接受的理由
senses.example: The delay was justified by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误因暴风雨而有其理由。
senses.why: Here the subject is the reason itself, not the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这里作主语的是理由本身，而不是说话的人。

senses.title: To set text flush at the margins
senses.definition: in printing, to space text so that both edges line up
senses.definitionCN: 排版中调整字距，使左右两边都对齐
senses.example: The columns are justified so the page looks tidy.
senses.exampleCN: 各栏都两端对齐，页面显得整齐。
senses.why: Typesetting sets lines to exact margins, the same exactness the word always carried.
senses.whyCN: 排版把行对齐到精确的边界，正是这个词一直带有的「精确」。

senses.title: To prove oneself right by result
senses.definition: to be shown right by later events
senses.definitionCN: 指后来的事实说明当初是对的
senses.example: The final score justified the coach's choice.
senses.exampleCN: 最终比分证明了教练的选择。
senses.why: Later facts can do the weighing that argument could not.
senses.whyCN: 后来发生的事实能做论证做不到的那次称量。

senses.title: To declare someone righteous
senses.definition: in theology, to declare a person righteous before God
senses.definitionCN: 神学中指宣告某人在神面前为义
senses.example: The doctrine says faith alone justifies the believer.
senses.exampleCN: 该教义说唯凭信使信徒称义。
senses.why: The theological sense is a declaration of rightness rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 神学义是一种宣告其为义，而不是去证明。

intro.en: Justify is Latin justus, right, plus facere, to make: to make right or to show as right.
intro.cn: justify 是拉丁语 justus「正当的」加 facere「做」：使之正当，或显示其为正当。

items.en: justificare meant to make just or to do justice, from justus and facere.
items.cn: justificare 意为使之公正或伸张正义，由 justus 与 facere 组成。

items.en: The -fic- element is a form of facere, to make or do.
items.cn: -fic- 部分是 facere「做」的形式，广见于 -ify 动词。

items.en: English borrowed justify in the fourteenth century for legal defence.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 justify，最初用于法律辩护。

items.en: The theological sense of being declared righteous developed in the Reformation.
items.cn: 「称义」的神学义在宗教改革时期发展起来。

items.en: The printing sense arrived with mechanical typesetting.
items.cn: 排版义随机械排字而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ify pattern and the justice root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of defending and explaining.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ify 构词与 justice 词根；近义组收辩护与解释类动词。

entries.definition: Fairness or the court system.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「正义；司法」。

entries.definition: One who gives a defence.
entries.definitionCN: 由 justify 加 -er 构成，指辩解者。

entries.definition: A reason given in defence.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「正当理由」。

entries.definition: To protect or argue for something attacked.
entries.definitionCN: 指抵御或为受攻者辩护。

entries.definition: To make something clear.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事情说清楚，不必涉及对错。

entries.definition: To try to lessen the blame for something.
entries.definitionCN: 指为减轻过错找借口。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from justus plus facere to justified text on a page.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 justus 加 facere 走到页面上两端对齐的文字。

normal.en: Justify is just plus -ify, which comes from facere, to make.
normal.cn: justify 是 just 加 -ify，后者来自 facere「做」。

normal.en: The -ify ending also appears in testify and simplify.
normal.cn: -ify 词尾也见于 testify 与 simplify。

normal.en: Justify doing something is the common pattern.
normal.cn: justify doing something 是常见搭配。

normal.en: The noun is justification, not justifation.
normal.cn: 名词是 justification，不是 justifation。

normal.en: Justified text lines up on both sides.
normal.cn: justified text 指左右两边都对齐的文字。

abstract.en: To justify is to hand the scale a weight that balances.
abstract.cn: 辩护就是往秤另一头放上配得上的砝码。

abstract.en: A reason that fits exactly is justice at the level of argument.
abstract.cn: 恰好配平的理由，就是论证层面的正义。

abstract.en: Some things cannot be weighed at all.
abstract.cn: 有些事根本没法上秤。

examples.en: Nothing can justify hiding the report.
examples.cn: 没有任何理由能为隐瞒报告开脱。

examples.en: She was justified in refusing the offer.
examples.cn: 她拒绝这个提议是有道理的。

examples.en: Justify the whole paragraph to make it look clean.
examples.cn: 把整段两端对齐，看起来更整齐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「just 我 fi」—— 站得正，才敢说「我没错」

root: 拉丁语 justus「正当的」+ facere「做」→ justificare「使之正当」→ 英语 justify；名词 justification。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: showing something right, defending it, being the reason for it, aligning text, being proved right, and being declared righteous.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：证明合理、为决定辩护、构成理由、文字两端对齐、以结果证明，以及宗教上的「称义」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reasons laid on a scale until it balances.
core.cn: 核心意象：把理由放到秤上，直到配平。

branches.en: THE SCALE: reasons heavy enough to hold the act up.
branches.cn: 秤这条线：理由够重，撑得住那个行为。

branches.en: THE MEETING: a decision explained to those who question it.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：向质疑者解释决定。

branches.en: THE PAGE: every line lands on both margins.
branches.cn: 页面这条线：每一行都落在两边边界上。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: the result that settles the argument.
branches.cn: 记分牌这条线：结果把争论定下。

branches.en: THE PULPIT: the doctrine of being made righteous.
branches.cn: 讲坛这条线：称义的教义。

intro.en: Justify is just plus the Latin verb ending -ify, from facere.
intro.cn: justify 是 just 加拉丁动词词尾 -ify，源自 facere。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from jus through justus and from facere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词来自 jus（经 justus）与 facere。
